data.title: Command-stream primitive encoders + AddressTable + pack_config (core leaf)
data.body:
## Goal
- Land the pure-Rust **command-stream primitives** leaf: opcode/sentinel constants,
  `AddressTable`, `pack_config`/`pack_expected_balance`, `enc_preamble`, the
  `enc_erc20_*`/`enc_weth_*`/`enc_send_eth*` (0x10–0x17), the `enc_v2_swap_*`
  (0x20–0x22 incl. forward_data), the `enc_v3_swap_*` (0x30–0x31), the
  `enc_v4_swap_*`/`enc_v4_batch` (0x40–0x42), the V4 settlement/ERC6909 opcodes
  `enc_v4_unlock/take/take_compact/take_delta/sync/settle/settle_delta/settle_all/mint_compact/burn_compact`
  (0x50–0x59), and `make_pool_key`.
- PyO3-free core. This is the building block for the path composers (the sibling 2-hop /
  3-hop composer tasks depend on it).

## Context
- Scope task: `E7GB27` (epic `WWC4DL`).
- Rubric dispositions: rows A1–A11 are all `port-now` (smell #1 — 1:1 port of a deployed
  Vyper contract's command layout; pure byte/int transforms; hot per-tx dispatch path;
  no I/O; no Python-ecosystem coupling beyond `eth_abi` which `degenbot-abi::encode_rust`
  already covers).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1 (pure-Rust
  core leaf), `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md` (standalone-
  core constraint + zero-`pyo3`-in-cores), `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md` §10
  (the 9 path types + their payload sequences), §10.2 (V3 vs V4 sign conventions — V4
  uses negative `amountSpecified`; the compact uint96 is positive and the contract
  negates internally), §10.3 (`NATIVE_ADDRESS` handling).
- Python oracle (parity source of truth until §4.2 passes): `examples/cmd_stream.py`
  (constants L60–L113; `_e`/`_address_to_bytes` L122–L150; `AddressTable` L178–L265;
  `pack_config`/`pack_expected_balance` L137–L184; `enc_preamble`/`enc_set_address`/
  `enc_set_addresses` L269–L329; the `enc_*` opcode builders L334–L891; `make_pool_key`
  L898–L918). Contract layout reference: `contracts/README.md` "Command-Stream Executor"
  table (opcode | name | encoding | description) — the authoritative spec; source in
  `~/code/executor/contracts/cmd_executor.vy`.
- Precedent: `rust/crates/degenbot-uniswap/src/v2_encoding.rs` (`encode_v2_swap`/
  `EncodedCall`/`V2_SWAP_SELECTOR`) is the template — same `degenbot-abi::encode_rust` +
  selector convention; `rust/crates/degenbot-uniswap/src/create2.rs` mirrors the
  currency-sort for `make_pool_key`.
- Crate placement: recommended **new core crate `degenbot-executor`** (pyo3-free, depends
  on `alloy` + `degenbot-abi` + `degenbot-core` + `degenbot-uniswap`); mirror the
  `degenbot-uniswap` precedent (domain-honest home, not foundational). Confirm with
  `t-6486` if a `degenbot-abi::cmd_stream` submodule is preferred instead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Address`, `U256`/`u128`/`u96`-shaped pure-Rust functions returning `Vec<u8>` (or
  `Result<Vec<u8>, E>`) for every opcode in the A1–A11 rows, named with plain `pub fn`
  (no `Py` prefix, no `#[pyfunction]` in the core).
- `AddressTable` struct: insertion-ordered dedup, sentinel map (`PM`/`SELF`/`WETH`/
  `NATIVE` = `0xFC`–`0xFF`), 32-entry cap (`MAX_INDEXED_ADDRESSES`), `.add`/`.index_of`/
  `.addresses`.
- `pack_config(check_mode, expected_value, bribe_bips, bribe_recipient_idx) -> U256` with
  the documented bit layout (bits 0–7 check_mode, 8–23 bribe_bips, 24–31
  bribe_recipient_idx, 32–255 expected_value) + input asserts.
- `make_pool_key` sorting currencies lexicographically (match `create2` precedent).
- V4 compact-amount encoders take a **positive** uint96 amount (the contract negates to
  negative `amountSpecified`) — documented in the fn docstring; tick_spacing as signed
  i16.
- `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests: byte-for-byte parity against the Python encoders over a
  fixture corpus (build from `examples/cmd_stream.py` outputs). `proptest`
  roundtrip/property tests where the shape admits it (address-table dedup, sentinel
  resolution, cap behaviour, bit-packing roundtrip).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (cargo test over the new crate).
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` — the new crate must be pyo3-free under default
  features.
- `just lint-rust` (clippy `--deny warnings`).
- Byte-for-byte parity check vs the Python `enc_*` encoders in
  `examples/cmd_stream.py` (red-green §4.2 — Python stays as the parity oracle here;
  deletion happens in the cutover task, not this one).

## Non-goals
- The per-path-type composers (`_encode_cmd_*`, `_3hop_*`, `V4V4ArbitragePayload`,
  `CmdExecutorComposer`) — sibling tasks.
- PyO3 wrappers + routing the example's `encode_cmd_stream` callsites through Rust —
  cutover task.
- ABI-encoding the outer `execute(bytes,uint256)` wrap (that's `degenbot-abi::encode_rust`,
  already done — E2) though `Command`/`EncodedCall` value types may be defined here if
  convenient.
- The warmup-slot math (`mapping_slot`/`compute_simulation_warmup_slots`) — sibling task.

data.title: degenbot-db core crate: SQLite connection + schema + typed rows + migration runner
data.body:
## Goal
- Land a new pyo3-free core crate `degenbot-db` (`rust/crates/degenbot-db/`) that owns the **SQLite persistence substrate** for the degenbot Rust core: connection/pool management, the schema DDL (mirroring the current Alembic head), typed row structs for every table, low-level read/write row functions, and a migration runner that can open an existing Alembic-stamped SQLite DB without clobbering its revision.
- This is the foundation (route-before-type, sub-step A of the rubric §3) onto which the snapshot-read cutover (sibling task), the builder-read cutover (sibling task), and the file-ops cutover (sibling task) route.

## Context
- Scope task: `5DU4QI` (Epic `VGTEDL` "Database persistence → Rust core").
- Rubric disposition for the substrate: **port-now**. No Rust DB counterpart exists today (`ls rust/crates/` — no `degenbot-db`; only `degenbot-bot` touches "snapshot" as in-memory verify seeds, not SQLite). The persistence responsibility is currently pure Python SQLAlchemy (`src/degenbot/database/{operations,session_manager}.py`, `models/*.py`, `migrations/`).
- §2.1 criteria driving `port-now`: type shape is pure numeric/byte/Address/U256 (tick→int, liquidity_gross/net→U256, address→checksum) — ideal Rust; standalone-Rust-core constraint (ADR-005) means a `cargo add degenbot` consumer doing backfill/snapshot reads needs persistence in a core crate from day one; I/O shape is pure transform (rows→structs) for the read fns.
- §2.3 smell: the snapshot readers hand-slice/serialize EVM integers via the `IntMappedToString` `TypeDecorator` (`models/base.py`) — a Rust typed row with `U256` columns removes that.
- The held `db: Option<Py<PyAny>>` on `PyBotIo` (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/py_bot_io.rs`) is the staged-but-inert routing seam — its docstring says "Slice 14c routes DB queries through here." This task builds the core that 14c routes to.
- Schema source of truth (mirror exactly): `src/degenbot/database/models/{base,types,erc20,pools,aave}.py` + `src/degenbot/migrations/versions/` head.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New crate `rust/crates/degenbot-db/` with `Cargo.toml` (`sqlx` with `sqlite` feature, or `rusqlite` — pick one and record the choice in `rust/CONTEXT.md`), `lib.rs`, and modules for: connection/pool (`SqliteConnection`/`Pool`), schema (embedded DDL via `sqlx::migrate!` or `refinery`, matching the Alembic head), typed row structs (`ExchangeRow`, `Erc20TokenRow`, `LiquidityPoolRow` + per-DEX subclass discriminator via `kind`, `LiquidityPositionRow`, `InitializationMapRow`, `PoolManagerRow`, `ManagedLiquidityPoolRow`, `ManagedPoolLiquidityPositionRow`, `ManagedPoolInitializationMapRow`, Aave tables), read fns (`fetch_pool_by_address`, `fetch_token_by_address`, `fetch_liquidity_map(pool_address)`, `fetch_all_liquidity_maps(chain_id)`, `fetch_pools_for_chain`, `fetch_newest_update_block`), write fns (`upsert_erc20_token`, `upsert_pool_row`, `upsert_liquidity_positions`, `set_liquidity_update_marker`).
- U256/big-int columns map losslessly (mirror `IntMappedToString`'s VARCHAR(78) string round-trip OR use a native big-int SQLite representation — record the choice; must round-trip the full 32-byte EVM range).
- The migration runner, pointed at an existing degenbot SQLite DB, reads the `alembic_version` table head and treats an already-stamped DB as current without re-running DDL.
- `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests: round-trip insert→read for each row type against a `:memory:` sqlite; parity fixture reading a fixture SQLite file produces the same `LiquidityMap`/tick dicts as the Python `DatabaseSnapshot.get_liquidity_map`.
- **Zero `pyo3`** in the crate (enforced by `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`).
- Workspace virtual manifest `rust/Cargo.toml` lists the new member; `degenbot` umbrella re-exports it (or not, per publish-deferred state — at minimum it builds as a workspace member).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` — new crate unit + integration tests pass.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` — still PASS (crate is pyo3-free).
- `just lint-rust` — clippy `--deny warnings` clean on the new crate.

## Non-goals
- PyO3 bindings / `#[pyclass]` surface (that is the sibling routing tasks under `degenbot-python`).
- Routing the Python `DatabaseSnapshot` / builders / CLI through Rust (sibling tasks).
- The DB-aware **writer/orchestration** logic (the `UniswapV3LiquiditySnapshot.update` fetch-and-persist loop, CLI bulk updaters, Aave `db_*` updaters) — that is Epic `AZGJUN` (Scope `MPS3U7`), which depends on this substrate.
- Retiring the Python SQLAlchemy ORM / Alembic (kept as parity oracle + for writer paths until AZGJUN migrates them).

data.title: 2-hop + N-hop command-stream path composers (8 path types + V2N)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the **2-hop + N-hop command-stream path composers** to Rust: `encode_cmd_stream`
  top-level dispatcher, `_encode_cmd_v2_n_hop`, the eight `_encode_cmd_*` 2-hop functions
  (`_encode_cmd_v4_v4`, `_encode_cmd_v4_v3`, `_encode_cmd_v3_v4`, `_encode_cmd_v4_v2`,
  `_encode_cmd_v2_v4`, `_encode_cmd_v3_v3`, `_encode_cmd_v2_v3`, `_encode_cmd_v3_v2`),
  the `v4_input_is_native`/`v4_output_is_native` helpers, and the dataclass payloads
  `V4V4ArbitragePayload`/`V4V3ArbitragePayload`/`CmdExecutorComposer` (the
  `PayloadComposer`-protocol impl that ABI-wraps the stream in `execute(bytes,uint256)`).
- Composes the primitives from the sibling core-leaf task into a complete command-stream
  `bytes` payload per path type, returning `Option<bytes>` on unsupported/failing paths
  (Python returns `None`).

## Context
- Scope task: `E7GB27` (epic `WWC4DL`), rows B1/B2/B4/B5/B6.
- Rubric dispositions: all `port-now` (smell #1 — on-chain command-layout port; pure
  byte/int compose over the primitives; hot per-tx dispatch; no I/O; integer-only;
  `try/except → None` maps to Rust `Result`/`Option`).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1/§4.2,
  `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md` §10.1 (the 9 two-hop path types + payload
  sequences), §10.2 (V3 vs V4 sign conventions — V4 compact amounts are positive uint96,
  contract negates; V3 positive `amountSpecified`), §10.3 (`NATIVE_ADDRESS` /
  `address(0)` ≡ WETH for direction, and the executor wraps ETH→WETH via
  `IWETH.deposit()` during settlement), §9 (the executor's V3 auto-pay + V4
  unlock/settle/take/sync flow).
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py` — `encode_cmd_stream` L533–L665,
  `v4_input_is_native`/`v4_output_is_native` L667–L678, `_encode_cmd_v2_n_hop` L679–L780,
  `_encode_cmd_v4_v4` L782–L1005, `_encode_cmd_v4_v3` L1007–L1140,
  `_encode_cmd_v3_v4` L1142–L1290, `_encode_cmd_v4_v2` L1292–L1433,
  `_encode_cmd_v2_v4` L1435–L1575, `_encode_cmd_v3_v3` L1577–L1657,
  `_encode_cmd_v2_v3` L1659–L1742, `_encode_cmd_v3_v2` L1744–L1840. Dataclass builders:
  `examples/cmd_stream.py` `V4V4ArbitragePayload` L963–L1140, `V4V3ArbitragePayload`
  L1400–L1612, `CmdExecutorComposer` L1461–L1652 (the `_encode_v4_v4` there is the 9th
  two-hop combo, dispatched via `SwapAmounts` not HopInfo).
- Input shape: the encoder consumes `optimal_input` + `hop_outputs` (engine results,
  already Rust-owned) + hop identity (`pool_address`/`pool_key`, `fee`, `tick_spacing`,
  `currencies`, `zfo`) — all handle-readable via `PyLiquidityPool` (E4). Defines a
  Rust-side hop descriptor struct mirroring the Python `V2HopInfo`/`V3HopInfo`/`V4HopInfo`
  (carrying the per-hop identity the composer needs; see `src/degenbot/arbitrage/hop_info.py`).
- Parity required (§4.2) — Python stays as the oracle until byte-for-byte cross-check
  passes; deletion happens in the cutover task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `encode_cmd_stream(...) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` dispatcher matching the Python
  path-type routing (n-hop V2; 2-hop V4-V4/V4-V3/V3-V4/V4-V2/V2-V4/V3-V3/V2-V3/V3-V2).
- `_encode_cmd_v2_n_hop` for N≥2 V2 hops (flash borrow + chained `V2_SWAP_CALC` with
  direct custody + flash repayment), including the address-table-index-hygiene guard
  noted in `contracts/README.md` design decision 8.
- Each 2-hop composer handles the documented settlement cases (e.g. V4-V4 same-currency
  delta-netting vs WETH↔native wrap/unwrap; V4-V3 auto-pay vs explicit forward_data;
  V3-V4 nested unlock; V4-V2/V2-V4 take+settle+transfer; V3-V3/V2-V3/V3-V2 token
  transfers + nested callbacks).
- V4 settlement opcodes composed inside `V4_UNLOCK` (sync/settle/take/take_delta/
  settle_delta/settle_all/mint_compact for ERC6909 profit) per the path's needs.
- `CmdExecutorComposer` analog that ABI-wraps the produced `commands` in
  `execute(bytes,uint256)` via `degenbot-abi::encode_rust` with the `execute` selector
  (`Web3.keccak(text="execute(bytes,uint256)")[:4]`).
- `#[cfg(test)]` byte-for-byte parity tests vs the Python encoders over a path-type
  fixture corpus (one fixture per path type × native/WETH/ERC20-Intermediate variants).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- `just test-rust-python` once the cutover task exposes the seam.
- Byte-for-byte parity check vs the Python `_encode_cmd_*` functions (§4.2 red-green).

## Non-goals
- The 3-hop composers (27 `_3hop_*` patterns + `_encode_cmd_3_hop`) — sibling task.
- The primitive `enc_*` opcode builders + `AddressTable` + `pack_config` — sibling
  core-leaf task (depends on it).
- PyO3 wrapper + routing the example's `encode_cmd_stream` through Rust + deleting the
  Python encoder — cutover task.
- The warmup-slot math — sibling task.

## Dependencies
- Depends on the command-stream primitives core-leaf task (opcode builders +
  `AddressTable` + `pack_config` + `make_pool_key`).

data.title: Route V3/V4 snapshot DatabaseSnapshot readers through degenbot-db
data.body:
## Goal
- Route the V3/V4 snapshot **DB readers** (`src/degenbot/uniswap/v3_snapshot.py::DatabaseSnapshot`, `v4_snapshot.py::DatabaseSnapshot`) through the new `degenbot-db` core crate (sibling task `SLHSM4`) via a thin `#[pyclass]`/`#[pyfunction]` seam in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/`, and convert the Python `DatabaseSnapshot` classes into delegating shells (rubric §3 sub-steps B + C).

## Context
- Scope task: `5DU4QI` (Epic `VGTEDL`). Rubric disposition for the snapshot read path: **port-now**.
- §2.1 criteria: I/O shape = pure row→struct transform (no Python-ecosystem coupling beyond the SQLAlchemy call itself); type shape = int/Address/U256; not a per-block hot path (startup backfill only — `rust-owned-bot.md` §6.6 backfill_snapshots) but a bulk read where Rust's zero-allocation decode matters (`get_all_liquidity_maps` raw-SQL bulk path). Standalone constraint: a `cargo add degenbot` consumer doing backfill must read snapshots from a Rust crate.
- §2.3 smell: the readers hand-build a `LiquidityMap`/`tick_data` dict + a raw-SQL `get_all_liquidity_maps` to avoid ORM overhead — a Rust typed-row reader collapses both into one seam.
- Depends on `SLHSM4` (`fetch_liquidity_map`, `fetch_all_liquidity_maps`, `fetch_pools`, `fetch_newest_update_block`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New PyO3 module `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/` with `#[pyclass] PyDatabaseSnapshot` (or `#[pyfunction]`s) holding a `degenbot_db::SqliteConnection`/pool handle; registered in `c_api.rs`.
- Thin translator only: extract args → `py.detach()` (DB I/O) → call core → wrap result into Python types (`LiquidityMap`/`BitmapAtWord`/`LiquidityAtTick` TypedDicts, or raw tuples — match the existing return shapes so callers are unchanged).
- Python `DatabaseSnapshot` (both v3 + v4) delegates every method (`get_liquidity_map`, `get_all_liquidity_maps`, `get_newest_block`, `get_pools`) to the Rust seam; the SQLAlchemy `session.scalar/select` bodies deleted.
- Parity: a test fixture SQLite DB read through the Rust seam returns byte-identical `LiquidityMap`/tick dicts and the same `get_newest_block`/`get_pools` results as the prior Python path (red-green per §4.2 — keep the Python path as oracle until parity lands, then delete it per §4.3).
- `_DelegateSpy`-style delegation assertion (§4.5) proving the Python reader hits Rust with the right args.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (core crate tests), `just test-rust-python` (PyO3-wrapped tests), `just test-python` (snapshot reader tests), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- The `degenbot-db` crate itself (sibling `SLHSM4`).
- Routing builder/erc20-construction DB reads (sibling `C`).
- The `MonolithicJsonFileSnapshot` / `IndividualJsonFileSnapshot` alternate sources (stay Python — file-JSON orchestration, not SQLite persistence).
- Writer/snapshot-update orchestration (Epic `AZGJUN`).

data.title: Route builder/erc20/pathfinding construction-time DB reads through PyBotIo.db (slice 14c)

## Goal
- Route the **construction-time DB reads** in the pool/erc20 builders and pathfinding through `degenbot-db` via the `PyBotIo.db` seam (the "slice 14c routes DB queries through here" follow-through), converting the SQLAlchemy `db.scalar(select(...))` hydration callsites into delegating shells over Rust.

## Context
- Scope task: `5DU4QI` (Epic `VGTEDL`). Rubric disposition: **port-now**.

The `PyBotIo` Rust pyclass already holds `db: Option<Py<PyAny>>` inertly (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/py_bot_io.rs`) — this task makes it live (rubric §3.2 sub-step B, the binding layer, then §3.3 route + retire the Python query).
- Callsites to route (from `rg 'self\.db|db_session|session\.scalar|select\(.*Table'`): `src/degenbot/builders/{v2_builder_base,v3_builder_base,v4_builder_base,erc20_builder,async_erc20_builder,async_v2_pool_builder,async_v3_pool_builder,async_v4_pool_builder,type_resolution}.py`, `src/degenbot/erc20/erc20.py`, `src/degenbot/pathfinding.py`.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just test-python` (builder + erc20 + pathfinding suites), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

data.title: Port SQLite file ops (create/backup/compact/upgrade) into degenbot-db; CLI delegates
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the SQLite **file operations** (`create_new_sqlite_database`, `backup_sqlite_database`, `compact_sqlite_database`, `upgrade_existing_sqlite_database` in `src/degenbot/database/operations.py`) into `degenbot-db` (sibling `SLHSM4`), and convert the Click CLI (`src/degenbot/cli/database.py`: `backup`/`reset`/`upgrade`/`compact`) into a delegating shell over the Rust seam.

## Context
- Scope task: `5DU4QI` (Epic `VGTEDL`). Rubric split:
  - The SQLite file ops (create-with-WAL/`VACUUM`/Alembic stamp, `sqlite3.Connection.backup`, `VACUUM`, `command.upgrade`) = **port-now** — pure SQLite/file I/O with no Python-ecosystem coupling beyond the Alembic `command` shim; a standalone Rust consumer needs DB create/upgrade/backup/compact.
  - The Click CLI commands (`cli/database.py`) = **stays-python** — CLI orchestration is a Python shell concern (rubric §2.1 "Keep in Python": orchestration).
- §2.1 for the ops: hot path = construction/CLI only; type shape = file path + pragma strings; I/O shape = sqlite file ops. Standalone constraint: a `cargo add degenbot` consumer must be able to create/upgrade/back up its DB from Rust.
- Depends on `SLHSM4` (the migration runner + connection the ops use).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `degenbot-db` exposes `create_new_database(path)`, `backup_database(src,dst)`, `compact_database(path)`, `upgrade_database(path)` (the Rust core already owns connection + migration runner from `SLHSM4`).
- A `#[pyfunction]` seam in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/db/` wraps each op (registered in `c_api.rs`); `py.detach()` for the file I/O.
- `cli/database.py`'s four commands delegate to the Rust seam; the inline `create_engine`/`sqlite3.connect`/`command.upgrade` bodies in `operations.py` deleted (functions kept as thin Python wrappers or removed if the CLI calls Rust directly).
- `backup_sqlite_database`'s integrity-check assertions (`PRAGMA integrity_check`) preserved in Rust.
- Parity (§4.2): `degenbot database create/backup/compact/upgrade` against a fixture DB produces an equivalent file (WalMode, stamped to head, byte-stable backup) — keep Python path as oracle until green, retire per §4.3.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just test-python` (CLI database tests), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- The `degenbot-db` crate itself (sibling `SLHSM4`).
- The `DatabaseSettings` config / path resolution (`config.py`) — stays Python (config loading is a shell concern; the Rust core takes a resolved path).
- The Alembic migration **authoring** toolchain — stays Python (Alembic autogenerate is a Python-ecosystem dev tool); only the runtime migration **runner** ports (in `SLHSM4`).

data.title: Simulation warmup-slot / mapping_slot storage-slot math (core leaf)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the **simulation warmup-slot / `mapping_slot` storage-slot math** to Rust:
  `mapping_slot`, `_nested_mapping_slot`, `_keccak256`, and
  `compute_simulation_warmup_slots`.
- Produces the `eth_simulateV1` `stateDiff` overrides that replicate
  `cmd_executor.initialize()` (warms WETH9 `balanceOf(executor)` at slot 3 and
  PoolManager ERC6909 `balanceOf` at slot 4 nested-mapping slots for the WETH + native
  ids) so injected-runtime-bytecode simulations see warm storage.

## Context
- Scope task: `E7GB27` (epic `WWC4DL`), rows C1–C2.
- Rubric disposition: `port-now` (pure Solidity-mapping storage-slot math —
  `keccak256(key ‖ base_slot)`; integer-only; property-testable). `_keccak256` is trivially
  `alloy::primitives::keccak256`.
- Canonical references: `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md`
  (standalone-core constraint), `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1,
  `contracts/README.md` "cmd_executor immutables" + "Code Injection"
  (`rust/CONTEXT.md` {Code Injection} documents the runtime-bytecode injection flow this
  feeds).
- The slot-computation is pure (executor-address / WETH-address / PoolManager-address →
  nested-mapping slots). The OUTPUT is an `eth_simulateV1`-specific dict
  (`{address: {"stateDiff": {slot_hex: value_hex}}}`); the dict shape may keep a thin
  Python adapter at the boundary, but the slot math lands in a core crate.
- Python oracle: `examples/cmd_stream.py` — `mapping_slot` L884–L891, `_nested_mapping_slot`
  L894–L916, `compute_simulation_warmup_slots` L919–L1054 (embeds the storage-layout
  knowledge: WETH9 `balanceOf` at slot 3; PoolManager C3-linearized ERC6909 `balanceOf`
  at slot 4 after `owner`/`pendingOwner`/`isOperator`/`protocolFeesAccrued`; ERC6909 id =
  `uint160(currency)` per `CurrencyLibrary.toId()`).
- Existing test: `tests/arbitrage/test_warmup_slots_gas.py` (414 lines) — the parity
  corpus.
- Parity required (§4.2) — the slot math must match the Python output exactly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `mapping_slot(base_slot: U256, key: U256) -> U256` and
  `nested_mapping_slot(base_slot, key1, key2) -> U256` over `alloy::primitives::keccak256`.
- `compute_simulation_warmup_slots(executor, weth, pool_manager) -> WarmupSlots` returning
  the three computed slots (WETH9 balance slot, PoolManager ERC6909 WETH-id slot, native-id
  slot) as a typed struct (the `eth_simulateV1` dict shape can be built in a thin PyO3
  wrapper).
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests against `tests/arbitrage/test_warmup_slots_gas.py` fixture
  values (the WETH = `0xC02...` / PM = `0x0000...444c` mainnet slots are the canonical
  ground truth).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- Byte-for-byte parity check vs the Python `compute_simulation_warmup_slots` output.

## Non-goals
- The cmd-stream opcodes / path composers — sibling tasks.
- The `eth_simulateV1` call itself (Simulation epic `5LLJHX`) — this task only computes
  the slot overrides.
- PyO3 wrapping (cutover task) — though a thin PyO3 adapter that turns the typed struct
  into the `stateDiff` dict is in-scope for the cutover task, not here.

## Dependencies
- Standalone (pure keccak math). No dep on the opcode/primitive leaf, but co-located in
  the same `degenbot-executor` core crate if created.

data.title: Revert taxonomy (classify_revert) + thin-margin result filter (core leaf)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the **revert taxonomy** (`classify_revert` + `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` +
  `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS`) and the **thin-margin result filter**
  (`filter_thin_margin_results`) to Rust.
- `classify_revert(revert_data: &[u8]) -> &str` returns a stable label for cmd_executor +
  PoolManager revert selectors, `Error(string)`, `Panic(uint256)`, bare numeric Vyper
  reverts, or `unknown:0x........`; never raises. `filter_thin_margin_results` drops solver
  results whose `profit / opt_input` is below a BPS threshold.

## Context
- Scope task: `E7GB27` (epic `WWC4DL`), rows D1/D2.
- Rubric disposition: `port-now` (pure bytes→label / pure integer margin filter; never-
  raises contract; property-testable; no I/O).
  - **EPIC-PLACEMENT FLAG:** `classify_revert` straddles two contracts —
    `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS` are the cmd_executor's (affined to this epic), but
    `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` are the PoolManager's (affined to decode/Simulation). This
    epic `WWC4DL` BLOCKS the Simulation epic `5LLJHX`; the revert taxonomy may more
    naturally belong under `5LLJHX`. Created here because it is executor-affined and pure,
    but `t-6486` may transfer it. **Needs t-6486 confirmation.**
- `filter_thin_margin_results` is a pre-sim filter; it consumes engine results
  (`(path_id, opt_input, profit, hop_outputs, consumed_inputs, solve_block)` tuples). Also
  a candidate for `5LLJHX`. Flagged.
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1 (core leaf
  in `degenbot-decoders` for revert-data decode, or in `degenbot-executor` if that crate is
  created), §4.2 parity. `contracts/README.md` callback + error table for the selector
  list.
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py` — `classify_revert` L376–L417,
  `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` L357–L367, `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS` L369–L375,
  `_ERROR_STRING_SELECTOR`/`_PANIC_SELECTOR` L372–L374, `format_failure_breakdown`
  L419–L436 (rendering only — stays-Python display), `filter_thin_margin_results` L439–L477.
- `degenbot-decoders` covers *event* decode, not revert-data taxonomy — no Rust
  counterpart exists for these selectors.
- `format_sim_diag_line` (L479–L528) is `stays-python` (display/diagnostics, `json.dumps`
  + heterogeneous snapshot dict) — NOT in this task; flagged in the scope table so the next
  sweep does not re-litigate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `classify_revert(revert_data: &[u8]) -> &'static str` (or
  `Result<String, _>`) matching the Python taxonomy: `empty`, `short:<hex>`,
  `Panic(0x..)`, decoded `Error(string)`, selector-labels (params dropped) for the
  cmd_executor + V4 custom errors, `numeric-revert`, `unknown:0x........`. Never panics
  (malformed input returns a best-effort label).
- Selector constants (or a static map) for `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` +
  `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS`.
- `filter_thin_margin_results(results, min_profit_margin_bps) -> (kept, dropped_count)`
  with the integer-exact comparison `profit * BPS_DENOM >= opt_input * bps` (no float),
  matching the Python edge cases (`opt_input == 0` keeps; `<=0` threshold disables).
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests vs the Python functions over a revert-data fixture corpus.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- Byte/label parity check vs the Python `classify_revert` + `filter_thin_margin_results`.

## Non-goals
- `format_sim_diag_line` (stays-Python display).
- The full simulation pipeline (Simulation epic `5LLJHX`).
- PyO3 wrapper + routing `classify_revert` callsites through Rust (cutover task).

## Dependencies
- Standalone (pure data). Co-located in `degenbot-executor` (or `degenbot-decoders`) once
  that crate lands.

data.title: PyO3 wrapper + cutover: route encode_cmd_stream through Rust + retire Python encoder (parity §4.2, §4.3)
data.body:
## Goal
- **PyO3 wrapper + cutover:** expose the Rust command-stream encoding core
  (primitives + 2/N-hop + 3-hop composers + warmup-slot math + revert-taxonomy if
  transferred) through thin `#[pyfunction]`/`#[pyclass]` seams in
  `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/executor/`, route the example's `encode_cmd_stream` +
  `compute_simulation_warmup_slots` callsites through Rust, cross-check byte-for-byte
  against the Python encoder (red-green parity §4.2), then **delete the Python encoder** +
  its parity tests (oracle-retirement §4.3).

## Context
- Scope task: `E7GB27` (epic `WWC4DL`), cutover sub-steps §3.2 (PyO3 wrapper) → §3.3
  (route + delete).
- Rubric: this is the routing cutover. The Python encoder is the **parity oracle** until
  §4.2 byte-for-byte cross-check passes; then retire it WITH its parity tests
  (§4.3 — do not leave an equivalence harness comparing two live implementations).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.2 (thin
  PyO3 wrapper — arg extract → `py.detach()` → core call → result wrap; no business logic),
  §3.3 (route the companion through Rust + delete the Python port), §4.2 (red-green parity
  cross-check — the swap-encode port must be cross-checked byte-for-byte against the
  Python encoder before the Python port is deleted), §4.3 (oracle-retirement protocol),
  §4.5 (`_DelegateSpy` delegation-detection pattern to prove the seam, not just the
  numbers).
- Wrappers live in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/executor/` mirroring the
  `degenbot-executor` core crate; register every symbol in `c_api.rs`/`lib.rs`.
- Callsite to retarget: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` L1904 `encode_cmd_stream`
  (+ any `compute_simulation_warmup_slots` callsite). The retired Python functions live in
  `examples/cmd_stream.py` + `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Thin `#[pyfunction]`s (`encode_cmd_stream(...)`, `compute_simulation_warmup_slots(...)`,
  `pack_config(...)`, `classify_revert(...)`, `filter_thin_margin_results(...)` and/or a
  `#[pyclass]` `PyCmdExecutorComposer` carrying the executor/weth/pm config) that extract
  Python args → release GIL for the encode compute → call the core → wrap the result into
  `bytes`/`dict`/`str`. No business logic in the wrapper.
- `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` (and any other `rg encode_cmd_stream` callsite)
  routed through the Rust seam.
- Byte-for-byte parity test corpus over ALL path types (9 two-hop + 27 three-hop + V2N +
  native/WETH/ERC20-intermediate variants) green vs the Python oracle, for both
  `encode_cmd_stream` and `compute_simulation_warmup_slots`.
- After parity is green: delete `examples/cmd_stream.py`'s `enc_*`/`AddressTable`/
  `pack_config`/`mappping_slot`/`compute_simulation_warmup_slots`/
  `V4V4ArbitragePayload`/`V4V3ArbitragePayload`/`CmdExecutorComposer` and
  `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py`'s `encode_cmd_stream` + `_encode_cmd_*` +
  `_3hop_*` + `_encode_cmd_v2_n_hop` + `v4_input_is_native`/`v4_output_is_native` +
  `classify_revert` + `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` + `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS` +
  `filter_thin_margin_results`. Delete the parity tests with them (§4.3). Keep the
  `format_sim_diag_line` (stays-Python) and `format_failure_breakdown` (display-only
  rendering over the now-Rust `classify_revert` label — keep as a thin consumer of the
  Rust seam).
- `_DelegateSpy`-style test (§4.5) proving the example calls the Rust seam (not the
  deleted Python), where the shape admits it.
- `rust/CONTEXT.md` glossary entry for the new `degenbot-executor` crate +
  `{PyCmdExecutorComposer}`/`{encode_cmd_stream}` if a wrapper class is added.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`,
  `just lint-rust` (and `just lint-python` / `just format` for the example edits).

  deleted (§4.2).
- `rg encode_cmd_stream examples/ src/` shows no remaining Python implementation (only a
  thin re-export/import of the Rust symbol if ergonomics need it).

## Non-goals
- Implementing the core encode logic (this task wires + retires; the core lives in the
  sibling HATTU7 / HK5IHY / 5DLEAV / 62H23D / SYI3PG tasks).
- `format_sim_diag_line` — stays Python (display).
- Deploying a new executor contract; encoding tracks the deployed `cmd_executor.vy`
  layout.

## Dependencies

# Scope: Database persistence → Rust core

Epic `VGTEDL` · Scope task `5DU4QI` · Agent `t-5e22@degenbot`

Status legend: **COMPLETED** = Rust-owned + Python delegating · **IN-FIGHT** = partial (Rust exists, Python still authority somewhere) · **NOT-STARTED** = no Rust counterpart; rubric says belongs in Rust.

Rubric (§2.1) criteria shorthand: **hot** (per-block/per-tx loop?) · **GIL** (CPU-bound holds GIL?) · **type** (pure numeric/byte/Address/U256 vs heavy Python obj/ORM) · **I/O** (ORM query/WS vs pure transform) · **eco** (Python-ecosystem coupling: SQLAlchemy/web3/Click/Fraction) · **test** (clear I→O vs mocks/fixtures).

## COMPLETED

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) | Pointer |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | No DB persistence responsibility is Rust-owned yet. The held `db: Option<Py<PyAny>>` on `PyBotIo` is **inert** (stored but not routed) — explicitly the "14c will route through here" staging slot, not a port. | `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/py_bot_io.rs` |

## IN-FIGHT

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) | Python side | Rust side |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | None. There is no Rust DB counterpart whose Python callsite is partially routed. `PyBotIo.db` is held-but-inert (see COMPLETED note), not a partial port. The entire persistence responsibility is `NOT-STARTED`. | — | — |

## NOT-STARTED (`port-now` / `stays-python`)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SQLite connection + schema DDL + typed row structs + migration runner** (the persistence substrate) | `port-now` | type=pure int/Address/U256; I/O=row→struct transform; eco=low beyond the SQLAlchemy call; standalone constraint (ADR-005) — a `cargo add degenbot` consumer doing backfill needs a Rust DB. No Rust counterpart. | `src/degenbot/database/operations.py` (`get_scoped_sqlite_session`, `create_new_sqlite_database`); `session_manager.py::DatabaseSessionManager`; `models/{base,types,erc20,pools,aave}.py`; `migrations/{env.py,versions/}` | (none — `ls rust/crates/` has no `degenbot-db`) | `SLHSM4` |

CLI commands: orchestration → keeps Python. | `src/degenbot/database/operations.py::{create_new,backup,compact,upgrade_existing}_sqlite_database`; `src/degenbot/cli/database.py` | (none) | `OP23QV` (deps `SLHSM4`) |

Route-before-type ordering: `SLHSM4` lands the pyo3-free core (sub-step A), then `WKZ7ID`/`QVMWQC`/`OP23QV` (sub-steps B+C, the PyO3 routing + Python-shell cutover) fan out in parallel off it. The four routing children are mutually independent (B/C/D touch disjoint Python callsites).

## Open dependency / blocking questions

1. **Cross-epic edge `VGTEDL` → `AZGJUN` (DB-aware pool & lending-market updaters): wired.** The updaters literally need the `degenbot-db` substrate to write through (Rust-owned writer orchestration posting to a Rust-owned DB); an epic-level dep is correct. **Coarseness flag:** the epic-level edge blocks the *entire* updaters epic until the *entire* DB epic finishes — once `AZGJUN`/`MPS3U7` scope its children, a finer child edge (updaters depend only on `SLHSM4` + the relevant read/write fns, not on the CLI file-ops task `OP23QV`) may be desirable. Recommend the AZGJUN scope agent refine to `SLHSM4` → updaters-child rather than epic→epic.

2. **Cross-epic edge `VGTEDL` → `JW7KU6` (Pathfinding graph construction): wired.** Pathfinding reads discovered pools/tokens, currently hydrated partly from the DB snapshot layer (`pathfinding.py` is in `QVMWQC`'s callsite list). **Softer dependency:** pathfinding may ultimately read from `BotState` (already Rust-owned) rather than the DB, in which case the epic-level edge is too coarse. Recommend the JW7KU6 scope agent confirm whether pathfinding truly reads from DB at construction (hard dep on `QVMWQC`) or from `BotState` (no dep on this epic), and refine.

   **Note on prior state:** these two cross-epic edges were **absent** (`deps: None`) at scope time despite the coordinating agent (t-6486) noting they were "already wired" — I wired them here per the stated intent. If the coordinator intended a finer/child-level edge instead of epic-level, they can `ergo sequence rm VGTEDL AZGJUN` (and `rm VGTEDL JW7KU6`) and re-wire at child granularity once the consumer epics are scoped.

3. **sqlx vs rusqlite** — left as an implementation decision in `SLHSM4` (both satisfy the pyo3-free + standalone constraint). No blocker.

4. **Existing Alembic-stamped DB compatibility** — `SLHSM4` must read `alembic_version` and treat a stamped DB as current (the runtime runner ports; Alembic autogenerate stays Python). Recorded as an AC in `SLHSM4`, not a blocker.

- Scope table written into this task body before any implementation child task was created (AC met).

# Scope: Swap encoding (executor/command stream) → Rust core

Epic `WWC4DL` · Scope task `E7GB27`.
Rubric: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.1 (decision table) / §2.2
(four dispositions) / §2.3 (smell #1: 1:1 port of a deployed Vyper contract's command
layout → `port-now`). Cutover discipline §3.1 (pure-Rust core leaf) → §3.2 (PyO3 wrapper)
→ §3.3 (route + delete). Red-green parity §4.2: the Python encoder is the parity oracle
until byte-for-byte cross-check passes, THEN retire it with its parity tests (§4.3).

Confirmed baseline: `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` PASS (cores + umbrella pyo3-free under
default features) before any work.

## Summary disposition

The entire command-stream encoding responsibility is **pure byte/int transforms with no
I/O and no Python-ecosystem coupling** (selector constants, `int.to_bytes`, `keccak256`,
`bytes` concatenation). It is a 1:1 port of a deployed Vyper contract's
(`contracts/cmd_executor.vy`, source in `~/code/executor/`) command-bytecode layout. Per
rubric smell #1 + §2.1 (hot path? per-block, in the dispatch loop. GIL? CPU-bound, holds
GIL during encode. type shape? pure `Address`/`U256`/bytes. I/O? none.
Python-ecosystem coupling? `eth_abi` only at the outer `execute(bytes,uint256)` wrap, and
`degenbot-abi::encode_rust` already covers that. test shape? clear input→bytes,
property-testable roundtrip) → **`port-now`** for nearly every row. One
display/diagnostic row leans `stays-python`.

The single-hop V2 `swap()` calldata encoder (`degenbot-uniswap::v2_encoding`) is the
existing precedent/checkpoint (`done` for what it covers) but it is a **different
codepath** — it produces legacy per-pool `swap(uint256,uint256,address,bytes)` calldata,
**not** the multi-hop `cmd_executor` command stream, which is entirely absent from Rust.

## Scope table

Legend: status = NOT-STARTED / IN-FIGHT / COMPLETED (mapped to the AC's three buckets);
disposition = rubric §2.2 disposition.

### A. Command-stream primitives + address table + config packing

| # | Row | Python source | Rust counterpart | Status | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------------|--------|-------------|------------------|
| A1 | Opcode + sentinel constants (`CMD_*`, `SENTINEL_*`, `MAX_INDEXED_ADDRESSES`, `BEGIN_EXECUTION`) | `examples/cmd_stream.py` L60–L113 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure `const` data (`u8` opcodes, sentinel indices); 1:1 port of `cmd_executor.vy` command set. Hot path; no I/O; no Python coupling. |
| A2 | `_e`, `_address_to_bytes` int/addr→bytes helpers | `examples/cmd_stream.py` L122–L150 | `alloy::primitives` covers; trivial | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure byte transform; idiomatic Rust (`u256::to_be_bytes`, `Address::into_array`). |
| A3 | `AddressTable` (dedup, sentinel map, 32-entry limit) | `examples/cmd_stream.py` L178–L265 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure `(Vec<Address>, HashMap, sentinel map)`; no I/O; property-testable (dedup, cap, sentinel resolution). |
| A4 | `pack_config` / `pack_expected_balance` (check_mode/bribe/expected_value bit-packing) | `examples/cmd_stream.py` L137–L184 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure uint256 bit-packing matching `execute()` ABI param; integer-exact, no float. |
| A5 | `enc_preamble`, `enc_set_address`, `enc_set_addresses` | `examples/cmd_stream.py` L269–L329 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure byte builder over the address table; banishes the retired `0xFE` prefix and reserved opcodes. |
| A6 | `enc_erc20_*`, `enc_weth_*`, `enc_send_eth*` (ERC20/ETH commands 0x10–0x17) | `examples/cmd_stream.py` L334–L456 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure byte concat; uint96/uint256 amounts; 1:1 with `cmd_executor.vy` opcodes. |

### B. Path composers (the per-path-type `_encode_cmd_*` dispatchers)

| # | Row | Python source | Rust counterpart | Status | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------------|--------|-------------|-----------|
| B1 | `_encode_cmd_v2_n_hop` (generalized N-hop V2 flash-borrow + chained `V2_SWAP_CALC`) | `eth_backrun_helpers.py` L679–L780 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure byte composer over A6/A7; hot per-tx; integer-only; `try/except → None` maps to Rust `Result`. |

The 9th combo (V4-V4) is `V4V4ArbitragePayload`/`CmdExecutorComposer._encode_v4_v4` in `cmd_stream.py`. |
| B3 | `_encode_cmd_3_hop` dispatcher + 27 `_3hop_*` patterns (V2/V3/V4 × 3) + `_enc_v4_swap` helper | `eth_backrun_helpers.py` L1842–L3516 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | ~1,670 lines of pure composer logic; largest single chunk; 1:1 with on-chain patterns; integer-only. |
| B4 | `encode_cmd_stream` top-level dispatcher (path-type → composer; returns `None` on unsupported) | `eth_backrun_helpers.py` L533–L665 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure dispatch on hop types; the entry point consumed by the hot loop. |
| B5 | `v4_input_is_native` / `v4_output_is_native` (currency0/1 == address(0)) | `eth_backrun_helpers.py` L667–L678 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure boolean predicate; folds into the V4 hop descriptor used by the composer. |
| B6 | `V4V4ArbitragePayload`, `V4V3ArbitragePayload`, `CmdExecutorComposer` (dataclass builders) | `examples/cmd_stream.py` L957–L1652 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure composer structs; `CmdExecutorComposer` is the `PayloadComposer`-protocol impl that wraps the stream in `execute(bytes,uint256)` via `eth_abi.encode` (reusable via `degenbot-abi::encode_rust`). |

### C. Simulation-warmup storage-slot math

| # | Row | Python source | Rust counterpart | Status | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------------|--------|-------------|-----------|
| C1 | `mapping_slot`, `_nested_mapping_slot`, `_keccak256` | `examples/cmd_stream.py` L884–L916 | `alloy::primitives::keccak256` covers; trivial | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure Solidity-mapping storage-slot math (keccak256 of key‖slot); integer-only; property-testable. |
| C2 | `compute_simulation_warmup_slots` (WETH9 slot 3 + PoolManager ERC6909 slot 4 nested-mapping overrides; the `eth_simulateV1` `stateDiff` for cmd_executor.initialize()) | `examples/cmd_stream.py` L919–L1054 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure int→slot dict; executor-specific storage-layout knowledge (ERC6909 `toId()` = `uint160(currency)`); 1:1 with `cmd_executor.initialize()`. The output dict shape is `eth_simulateV1`-specific but the slot computation is pure. (Output wrapping may keep a thin Python adapter — flagged in child task.) |

### D. Revert taxonomy + result filtering (executor-affined decode/diagnostics)

| # | Row | Python source | Rust counterpart | Status | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------------|--------|-------------|-----------|
| D1 | `classify_revert` + `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` + `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS` (selector→label taxonomy for cmd_executor & PoolManager reverts) | `eth_backrun_helpers.py` L376–L417 | `degenbot-decoders` covers *event* decode, not revert-data taxonomy; none for these selectors | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure bytes→label; integer/hex only; never-raises contract; property-testable. **Epic-placement question:** half the selectors are the cmd_executor's (affined here), half are PoolManager's (affined to decode/Sim). Likely belongs under Simulation epic `5LLJHX` (which this epic blocks) OR a shared `degenbot-executor` decode leaf — flagged below. |
| D2 | `filter_thin_margin_results` (BPS margin filter over engine results) | `eth_backrun_helpers.py` L439–L477 | none | NOT-STARTED | `port-now` | Pure integer (`profit * BPS_DENOM ≥ opt_input * bps`) — trivial, no float. Small enough to fold into the Simulation epic rather than this one; flagged. |
| D3 | `format_sim_diag_line` (JSON diagnostic line `[sim-diag] {...}`) | `eth_backrun_helpers.py` L479–L528 | none | NOT-STARTED | `stays-python` | Display/diagnostics: builds a `json.dumps(..., default=str)` machine-parseable line from a heterogeneous snapshot dict. Infrequent (only on revert), `json`/dict ecosystem coupling, display-oriented — per §2.1 "Python-ecosystem coupling" + "I/O shape" criteria this stays in the Python companion. Pure-data extraction of snapshot fields could port, but the JSON-emission surface is Python display. |

### E. Existing Rust precedent (the `done` inventory — do NOT redo)

| # | Row | Rust source | Python consumer | Status | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|-----|-------------|-----------------|--------|-------------|-----------|
| E1 | Single-hop V2 `swap()` calldata (`encode_v2_swap`/`EncodedCall`/`V2_SWAP_SELECTOR`) | `rust/crates/degenbot-uniswap/src/v2_encoding.rs` | `PyLiquidityPool::encode_swap` / `PyBot::encode_swap` (`.pyi` L1198/L1609) | COMPLETED | `done` | Produces legacy per-pool `swap(uint256,uint256,address,bytes)` calldata (rarer `tstore_executor.vy` shape), NOT the multi-hop command stream. Byte-for-byte parity tests already in-file (`encode_v2_swap_matches_python_reference`). This is the precedent/template for the cmd-stream port — same `degenbot-abi::encode_rust` + selector pattern. |
| E2 | Generic ABI encode/decode leaves (`encode_rust`/`decode_rust`/`encode_single_rust`) + PyO3 wrappers | `rust/crates/degenbot-abi/src/{abi_encoder,abi_decoder}.rs`, `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/abi/{encoder,decoder}.rs` | `degenbot_rs.encode`/`decode` | COMPLETED | `done` | The outer `execute(bytes,uint256)` ABI wrap (B6/CmdExecutorComposer) reuses this; `proptest` roundtrip encode→decode is the standard invariant (§4.2). No new ABI infra needed. |
| E3 | DEX identity / V4 pool-key currency-sort precedent | `rust/crates/degenbot-uniswap/src/{dex_identity,create2,deployments}.rs` | `PyLiquidityPool` identity read through handle | COMPLETED | `done` | Precedent for the standalone-core placement of identity/preset data; `make_pool_key` (A11) mirrors `create2`'s currency sort. |
| E4 | `PyLiquidityPool`/`PyBot` handle identity (`pool_key`, fees, `tick_spacing`, addresses) | `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/` | `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py` builds `PathInfo`/`V*HopInfo` from engine results + handle reads | COMPLETED | `done` | The encoder's inputs (pool address / pool_key / fee / tick_spacing / currencies / zfo / opt_input / hop_outputs) are already Rust-owned/handle-readable; the port routes them straight into the Rust leaf with no Python state mirror. (rust-owned-bot.md §17 known-limitation "Python pool objects used for encoding" — this epic retires it.) |

## Child-task split (port-now / partial rows → implementation tasks)

Confirmed against the code (the 3-hop chunk alone is ~1,670 lines / 27 patterns — too
large to fold with 2-hop). Crate-placement recommendation: a **new core crate
`degenbot-executor`** (pyo3-free, depends on `alloy` + `degenbot-abi` + `degenbot-core` +
`degenbot-uniswap` for V4 pool-key sort) holding the cmd-stream primitives (A1–A11), the
path composers (B1–B6), and the warmup-slot math (C1–C2). PyO3 wrappers live in
`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/executor/`. This mirrors how `v2_encoding` lives in
`degenbot-uniswap` (domain-honest, not foundational) and keeps the executor-contract
encoding out of the generic ABI crate.

- **A1–A11** → child task: *Command-stream primitive encoders + AddressTable + pack_config (core leaf)*
- **B1, B2, B4, B5, B6** → child task: *2-hop + N-hop command-stream path composers*
- **B3** → child task: *3-hop command-stream path composers (27 patterns)*
- **C1–C2** → child task: *Simulation warmup-slot / mapping_slot storage-slot math*
- **D1–D2** → child task: *Revert taxonomy + thin-margin filter* (epic-placement flagged)
- **A/B/C port + route `encode_cmd_stream` callsites through Rust + retire Python encoder (§4.2 parity, §4.3 oracle-retirement)** → child task: *PyO3 wrapper + cutover (route + delete)*

## Open dependency / blocking questions

1. **D1/D2 epic placement.** `classify_revert` (`_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS` are the
   cmd_executor's; `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` are PoolManager's) and `filter_thin_margin_results`
   are revert/pre-sim-filter concerns. `WWC4DL` blocks `5LLJHX` (Simulation), so strictly
   the simulation-side revert taxonomy could be that epic's. **Recommendation:** create the
   child under `WWC4DL` now (it's executor-affined and pure), but note it as a candidate
   transfer to `5LLJHX` if that epic's scope covers revert decoding. Needs `t-6486`
   confirmation.
2. **`degenbot-executor` crate creation.** New core crate is the cleanest home; confirm
   this is acceptable vs. extending `degenbot-abi` (a `cmd_stream` submodule) or
   `degenbot-bot`. The standalone-core constraint (ADR-005) favours a domain-honest crate
   (`degenbot-executor`), matching the `degenbot-uniswap` precedent.
3. **No cross-epic code dependency** on `VGTEDL` (t-5e22's RPC epic) — encoding is pure
   transform with zero I/O. Confirmed disjoint.
4. **`examples/` ownership.** `encode_cmd_stream` lives in `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py`
   (not `src/degenbot/`). The cutover (route + delete) touches example code; confirm the
   retired Python encoder should leave a thin parity-oracle harness in `examples/` until
   deletion, or move the parity corpus into `tests/rust/` (rubric §4.3 prefers the
   latter).
5. **`format_sim_diag_line` (D3) `stays-python`.** Flagged for the next sweep so it isn't
   re-litigated — the JSON-emission surface is Python display.
## Child-task IDs (real, ergo-generated)

| ID | Title | Purpose |
|----|-------|---------|
| `HATTU7` | Command-stream primitive encoders + AddressTable + pack_config (core leaf) | The `enc_*` opcode builders (0x10–0x59), `AddressTable`, `pack_config`, `enc_preamble`, `make_pool_key`. Standalone-Rust core leaf. |
| `HK5IHY` | 2-hop + N-hop command-stream path composers (8 path types + V2N) | `encode_cmd_stream` dispatcher + `_encode_cmd_v2_n_hop` + the 8 two-hop `_encode_cmd_*` + `V4V4ArbitragePayload`/`V4V3ArbitragePayload`/`CmdExecutorComposer`. |
| `5DLEAV` | 3-hop command-stream path composers (27 patterns) | `_encode_cmd_3_hop` + 27 `_3hop_*` patterns + `_enc_v4_swap`. |
| `62H23D` | Simulation warmup-slot / mapping_slot storage-slot math (core leaf) | `mapping_slot` / `compute_simulation_warmup_slots` / `_nested_mapping_slot`. |
| `SYI3PG` | Revert taxonomy (classify_revert) + thin-margin result filter (core leaf) | `classify_revert` + selector maps + `filter_thin_margin_results`. (Epic-placement flagged — may transfer to `5LLJHX`.) |
| `YQORTM` | PyO3 wrapper + cutover: route encode_cmd_stream through Rust + retire Python encoder | Thin `#[pyfunction]`/`#[pyclass]` seams; route the example callsite; byte-for-byte parity §4.2; delete Python encoder + parity tests §4.3. |

## Dependency edges (ergo `sequence`)

```
HATTU7 (primitives) ─┬─► HK5IHY (2/N-hop) ─► 5DLEAV (3-hop) ─┐
                      │                                       ├─► YQORTM (cutover)
62H23D (warmup) ─────┼──────────────────────────────────────► │
SYI3PG (revert) ─────┴──────────────────────────────────────► ┘
```
Cutover (`YQORTM`) gates on primitives + 2/N-hop + 3-hop + warmup + revert-taxonomy;
3-hop (`5DLEAV`) gates on 2/N-hop (`HK5IHY`); 2/N-hop gates on primitives (`HATTU7`).
Warmup-slot (`62H23D`) and revert-taxonomy (`SYI3PG`) are standalone (pure data/hash).
Epic `WWC4DL` is a ROOT blocking `5LLJHX` (Simulation), `SHT6GE` (Transaction-submission),
`2F77C6` (Dead-mirrors-cleanup) — confirmed via `ergo show WWC4DL` rdeps; correct as
wired by `t-6486`. No child-level cross-epic refinement needed beyond the `SYI3PG`
placement question above.

data.title: Port liquidity-mapping math (apply_liquidity_mapping_update/flip_tick) into degenbot-cl-math
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the pure liquidity-mapping math — `apply_liquidity_mapping_update`, `flip_tick`, `get_tick_word_and_bit_position` (currently pure Python in `src/degenbot/calculations/concentrated_liquidity.py` + `src/degenbot/uniswap/v3_libraries/tick_bitmap.py`) — into the existing pyo3-free `degenbot-cl-math` crate as standalone pure functions over typed `LiquidityMap`/tick-bitmap structs. This is the math foundation the DB-aware pool updater (sibling task) routes through, and it collapses the §2.3 duplication with `degenbot-bot`'s hot-path `n` module.

## Context
- Scope task: `MPS3U7` (Epic `AZGJUN`). Rubric disposition: **port-now**.
- §2.1 criteria: type=pure int/uint128/I256/U256; I/O=none (pure CPU); **hot CPU** (the DB updater applies it per-event in a bulk backfill; the hot-path equivalent is per-tx). §2.3 smell: the same Solidity `TickBitmap`/liquidity-mapping logic exists in TWO places — pure-Python here (DB-updater-only) AND Rust in `degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/n.rs::apply_liquidity_to_tick_range` + `compute_tick_ranges` (hot path, over in-memory `BotState`). Lifting the pure math into `degenbot-cl-math` (a standalone core crate with zero pyo3/tokio today) gives ONE shared fn; the DB updater calls it via PyO3 and `degenbot-bot`'s `n` module can later be refactored to call it (follow-up, non-blocking).
- `degenbot-cl-math` public surface today is only low-level helpers (`mulmod`, `to_uint160`, `to_int128` in `cl_lib/functions.rs`); the tick-bitmap + liquidity-mapping fns are NOT yet exposed. `flip_tick`/`get_tick_word_and_bit_position` have NO Rust counterpart anywhere (`rg 'fn flip_tick|fn .*word.*position' rust/crates/` = empty).
- Only consumer of the pure-Python `apply_liquidity_mapping_update` is `cli/pool.py` (the DB updater) — confirmed `rg` (not called by the hot path).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `degenbot-cl-math` gains `pub fn get_tick_word_and_bit_position(tick, tick_spacing) -> (word, bit)`, `pub fn flip_tick(tick_bitmap: &mut HashMap<i32,BitmapWord>, tick, tick_spacing)`, `pub fn apply_liquidity_mapping_update(...) -> LiquidityMapUpdateResult` operating on typed structs (`BitmapAtWord { bitmap: u256-equivalent }`, `LiquidityAtTick { liquidity_gross: U128, liquidity_net: I256 }`), mirroring the Python signatures in `calculations/concentrated_liquidity.py`.
- PyO3 seam (`#[pyfunction]` in `degenbot-python/src/cl_lib/`) wraps `apply_liquidity_mapping_update` so Python can call it (enables green-parity cutover of the DB updater before/independent of the full substrate routing).
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity: Rust fn applied to a fixture tick-events list produces byte-identical `tick_bitmap`/`tick_data` dicts as the pure-Python `apply_liquidity_mapping_update` (keep Py as oracle per §4.2).
- **Zero `pyo3`** in `degenbot-cl-math` (enforced by `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (cl-math unit + parity tests), `just test-rust-python` (PyO3 seam), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.

## Non-goals
- Routing the DB updater (`apply_v3/v4_liquidity_updates`) itself through Rust + `degenbot-db` (sibling task, deps this).
- Refactoring `degenbot-bot`'s `n`/`apply_liquidity_to_tick_range` to call the new shared cl-math fn (§2.3 collapse follow-up — non-blocking; record as a note for the bot-core maintainers).
- The DB substrate (`SLHSM4`, Epic `VGTEDL`) — this task is pure math, no DB dependency.

data.title: Port V3/V4 DB-aware liquidity updater + pool discovery writers into Rust over degenbot-db; CLI driver stays Python
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the V3/V4 **DB-aware liquidity updater** (`cli/pool.py::apply_v3_liquidity_updates` / `apply_v4_liquidity_updates` — read pool row + positions → apply liquidity-mapping math → upsert positions + init maps + stamp `liquidity_update_block`/`liquidity_update_log_index`) and the **pool discovery writers** (`cli/pool_updater_configs.py::update_v2/v3/v4_pools` — scan PoolCreated, upsert pool/config rows, stamp `ExchangeTable.last_update_block`) into a Rust apply-and-persist core over `degenbot-db` + `degenbot-cl-math`, exposed via a PyO3 seam. The Python `pool_update` driver loop + RPC event fetch stay as the shell.

## Context
- Scope task: `MPS3U7` (Epic `AZGJUN`). Rubric disposition: **port-now** (the apply-and-persist core) / **stays-python** (the driver loop + RPC fetch).
- §2.1 criteria (apply-and-persist core): type=Address/int/U256; I/O= substrate read (pool row + `liquidity_positions` + `initialization_maps`) + math + substrate write (upsert/delete positions + init maps, set stamps); warm/bulk path (per-block chunk backfill, not per-tx hot loop). §2.3 smell: the apply function reconstitutes a `PoolLiquidityMap` from DB rows via ORM relationships, calls the (pure-Py, soon-Rust) math, then hand-writes chunked `sqlite_upsert(...).on_conflict_do_update` + `delete(...)` — a Rust typed-row substrate (`SLHSM4`) collapses the ORM reconstitution + the hand-rolled chunked upsert into one seam.
- **Orchestrator open question answered:** the feed-side updater reads/writes the **DB directly** (`pool_in_db.liquidity_positions`, `session.execute(sqlite_upsert(...))`), NOT `BotState`. The in-memory `BotState` liquidity maps (`n_update_by_pool_id` in `degenbot-bot`) are a SEPARATE path (hot-path swap solver) NOT synced by these updaters. Therefore: **hard DB-substrate dependency on `SLHSM4`; NO dependency on `QVMWQC`** (builder/construction reads — different callsite set, though both use `SLHSM4` read fns); **NO dependency on a BotState child**.
- Driver loop `pool_update` + `_pool_updater` + `get_v3/v4_liquidity_events`/`get_events_from_contract`/`fetch_logs_retrying` = **stays-python** (CLI orchestration shell + RPC event fetch; `degenbot-rpc` event-fetch port is a separate concern not in this epic).
- Deps: `SLHSM4` (substrate: `fetch_liquidity_map`, `upsert_liquidity_positions`, `set_liquidity_update_marker`, `upsert_pool_row`, pool-row upsert for discovery) + sibling math task (lifted `apply_liquidity_mapping_update` in `degenbot-cl-math`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Rust core (in `degenbot-db` or a new `degenbot-updaters` core module) exposes `apply_v3_liquidity_updates(conn, pool_address, liquidity_events, chain_id)` and `apply_v4_liquidity_updates(...)` over `degenbot_db::SqliteConnection` + `degenbot_cl_math::apply_liquidity_mapping_update`; the ORM reconstitution + chunked `sqlite_upsert`/`delete` bodies replaced by substrate calls (`upsert_liquidity_positions(pool_id, &positions)`, `upsert_initialization_maps(...)`, `delete_stale_positions(pool_id, &ticks)`, `set_liquidity_update_marker(pool_id, block, log_index)`).
- Pool discovery writers `update_v2/v3/v4_pools` route PoolCreated upserts through `degenbot_db::upsert_pool_row` / `upsert_erc20_token` / `set_exchange_last_update_block`.
- PyO3 seam (`#[pyfunction]` in `degenbot-python/src/updaters/` or `db/`) wraps each apply/discovery fn, registered in `c_api.rs`; `py.detach()` for the DB I/O.
- Python `apply_v3_liquidity_updates`/`apply_v4_liquidity_updates`/`update_v2/v3/v4_pools` become delegating shells; the inline SQLAlchemy `session.scalar/select`/`sqlite_upsert`/`delete` bodies deleted.
- The block/log-index ordering invariants (the `assert blockNumber >= last; logIndex > last` guards) preserved in Rust (return/panic on violation, matching current assertion behavior).
- Parity (§4.2): apply a fixture event sequence against a fixture DB → identical resulting `liquidity_positions`/`initialization_maps` rows + `liquidity_update_block` stamp as the prior Python path (Py as oracle until green, retire per §4.3). The SQLite 32766-variable chunking behavior preserved (or superseded by a substrate batch fn that respects the limit).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just test-python` (`cli/pool.py` + `pool_updater_configs` updater tests), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- The liquidity-mapping math itself (sibling math task in `degenbot-cl-math`).
- The `SLHSM4` substrate (Epic `VGTEDL`).
- The `pool_update`/`_pool_updater` driver loop + RPC event fetch (`get_v3/v4_liquidity_events`, `fetch_logs_retrying`) — stays Python (orchestration + RPC, RPC port is another epic).
- The `UniswapV3/4LiquiditySnapshot` in-memory event-fetcher/`update()` classes (`v3_snapshot.py`/`v4_snapshot.py`) — they apply events to in-memory maps, not DB; their DB-read half is Epic `VGTEDL` (`WKZ7ID`).
- Aave lending-market writers (sibling task).
- Syncing `BotState` in-memory liquidity maps with the DB (separate concern; the hot path owns its own).

data.title: Port Aave V3 lending-market DB writers (event handlers + get_or_create upserts) into Rust over degenbot-db; aave_update driver stays Python
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the Aave V3 **lending-market DB writers** — the per-event handlers (`cli/aave/event_handlers.py::_process_*` for `CollateralConfigurationChanged`/`EModeCategoryAdded`/`EModeAssetCategoryChanged`/`AssetCollateralInEmodeChanged`/`ReserveUsedAsCollateralEnabled`/…) and the `get_or_create_*` upsert helpers (`cli/aave/db_market.py`, `db_assets.py`, `db_users.py`, `db_positions.py`) — into a Rust apply-and-persist core over `degenbot-db`, exposed via a PyO3 seam. The Python `aave_update` driver loop + RPC event fetch stay as the shell.

## Context
- Scope task: `MPS3U7` (Epic `AZGJUN`). Rubric disposition: **port-now** (writer/handler core) / **stays-python** (`aave_update` driver + RPC fetch).
- §2.1 criteria (writer core): type=int/Address/big-int config bitmaps; I/O=substrate read (asset/user/config row by key) + substrate upsert (`get_or_create_e_mode_category`/`get_or_create_asset_config`/`get_or_create_user_collateral_config`/`get_or_create_position`); warm/bulk path (per-block chunk backfill). §2.3 smell: each handler does `session.scalar(select(...))` → mutate ORM obj → `session.add()` — a Rust typed-row substrate collapses the get-or-create + event-decode→upsert into one seam.
- The `_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` helper (`event_handlers.py`) is pure bit-decode math → port alongside into the core (pure CPU, no I/O).
- Deps: `SLHSM4` (substrate Aave row structs + `upsert_*`/`get_or_create_*` fns — `SLHSM4`'s AC includes "Aave tables"). NO dependency on the liquidity-mapping math sibling (Aave writers do their own state logic, not CL tick math). NO dependency on `BotState`.
- `aave_update` (`cli/aave/commands.py`) + RPC event fetch = **stays-python** (orchestration + RPC).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Rust core exposes per-event apply fns (`process_collateral_configuration_changed(conn, event)`, `process_e_mode_category_added(...)`, `process_emode_asset_category_changed(...)`, `process_asset_collateral_in_emode_changed(...)`, `process_reserve_used_as_collateral_enabled(...)`, …) + the `get_or_create_*` upsert primitives (`get_or_create_e_mode_category`, `get_or_create_asset_config`, `get_or_create_user_collateral_config`, `get_or_create_user`, `get_or_create_collateral_position`, `get_or_create_debt_position`, `get_or_create_erc20_token`) over `degenbot_db::SqliteConnection`, with `_decode_reserve_configuration_bitmap` ported as a pure fn.
- PyO3 seam wraps each; registered in `c_api.rs`; `py.detach()` for DB I/O.
- Python `_process_*` handlers + `get_or_create_*` become delegating shells; inline `session.scalar/select`/`session.add` bodies deleted.
- Parity (§4.2): replay a fixture Aave event sequence against a fixture DB → identical resulting rows vs the prior Python path (Py as oracle until green, retire per §4.3). The `db_verification.py` invariant checks (`verify_gho_discount_amounts`, `verify_stk_aave_balances`) still pass against Rust-written rows.
- **Zero `pyo3`** in `degenbot-db` (the core fns live there or in a new `degenbot-updaters` core module; the `#[pyfunction]` seam lives in `degenbot-python` only).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just test-python` (`cli/aave/` suite + verification), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- The `SLHSM4` substrate (Epic `VGTEDL`).
- The `aave_update` driver loop + RPC event fetch — stays Python.
- The Aave rehydrate/read-back (`DatabasePositionQuery` in `aave/analysis/orchestrator.py`) — sibling task.
- The pure liquidity-mapping math (sibling, `degenbot-cl-math`) — Aave writers don't use it.
- The Aave `operations.py`/`extraction.py`/`enrichment` analysis pipeline (in-memory event→state modeling) — separate from DB persistence.
