data.title: next_base_fee EIP-1559 base-fee math (core leaf — degenbot-evm-math OR degenbot-core)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port `next_base_fee` — the pure EIP-1559 base-fee formula — to a pure-Rust core leaf:
  `next_base_fee(parent_base_fee, parent_gas_used, parent_gas_limit, min_base_fee=None,
  base_fee_max_change_denominator=8, elasticity_multiplier=2) -> u128` (integers only, no
  float), matching the EIP-1559 reference implementation.

## Context
- Scope task: `P7AMWR` (epic `SHT6GE`), row N1.
- Rubric disposition: `port-now` (pure integer EVM math; hot per-block; no I/O; no float;
  property-testable round-trip + target-bound + min-clamp; standalone-Rust-usable).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1 (core leaf)
  + §4.2 (parity), `docs/adr/ADR-005` (standalone-core + zero-pyo3),
  `src/degenbot/calculations/evm_math.py` L17–L73 (the reference implementation + the EIP
  link in its docstring), EIP-1559 §the `base_fee_max_change_denominator`=8 /
  `elasticity_multiplier`=2 defaults.
- Python oracle: `src/degenbot/calculations/evm_math.py` `next_base_fee` L17–L73; called
  in `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` L2825 (`_apply_block_if_ready`) + L2920
  (`main()` start-phase). The `min_base_fee` arg supports non-Ethereum EIP-1559 chains
  (e.g. linea) — preserve it.
- **Cross-epic (REFERENCE, no hard edge):** CONSUMED by both Submission (N5/N6 fee
  finalization) AND the Simulation epic `5LLJHX` (`base_fee_next` for net-profit in
  `YL2MTH`). Per orchestrator ruling, fees are reference-not-hard-edge; N1 is OWNED here
  (the EIP-1559 formula is submission/block-clock-domain) and Simulation references it.
- Crate placement: recommended **new core crate `degenbot-evm-math`** (pure EVM math, not
  submission-specific — mirrors the `cl_msb`/`cl_lsb` precedent in `degenbot-core/src/`),
  OR fold into `degenbot-core`. NOT in `degenbot-submission` (consumed cross-epic).
  **Confirm with `t-6486`.**

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `pub fn next_base_fee(parent_base_fee, parent_gas_used, parent_gas_limit,
  min_base_fee: Option<u128>, base_fee_max_change_denominator, elasticity_multiplier)
  -> u128` with the EXACT branch logic (`gas_used == target` → flat; `> target` → +
  `max(delta,1)`; `< target` → − `delta`), integer-exact (no float), `min_base_fee`
  enforced when `Some`.
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests against `src/degenbot/calculations/evm_math.py` over a
  fixture corpus (mainnet block headers — the `base_fee_next` values the bot observes);
  `proptest` for the target-bound + min-clamp invariants.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- Byte/integer parity check vs the Python `next_base_fee` (§4.2 red-green).

## Non-goals
- Fee finalization (`maxFeePerGas`/`maxPriorityFeePerGas` — N5 child) / sign + broadcast
  (N4/N6) — submission-orchestration siblings.
- The block-clock `feeHistory` fetch (I2, `ZUZANP`) + the `block_priority_fees` ring
  (N3) — separate concerns; this leaf is the pure formula.
- Simulation's consumption of `base_fee_next` — Simulation epic `5LLJHX` REFERENCES this
  leaf; not re-scoped.

data.title: Dispatcher nonce/pool/task coordination state (claim/release nonce, pool mutual exclusion, active_tasks JoinSet, current_block by-ref clock, block_priority_fees ring prune, PathSuppression delegation)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the `Dispatcher` **nonce/pool/task coordination state** to Rust: nonce claim/release
  (`claim_nonce`/`release_nonce` over a `pending_nonces: HashSet<u64>`), pool mutual
  exclusion (`reserve_pools`/`release_pools`/`is_path_blocked` against pending+committed
  pools), `active_tasks` (tokio `JoinSet` with auto-discard-on-completion), the
  by-reference `current_block` clock (`Arc<Mutex<u64>>` single-element pattern),
  `block_times` deque, the `block_priority_fees` ring (`FEE_HISTORY_WINDOW` prune +
  `latest_priority_fees`/`record_priority_fees`), and the `PathSuppression` delegation.

## Context
- Scope task: `P7AMWR` (epic `SHT6GE`), row N3.
- Rubric disposition: `port-now` (pure coordination state — `HashMap`/`HashSet` + a
  single-element `Arc<Mutex<u64>>` for the by-ref block clock; hot per-tx; GIL-held today
  across claim/release; property-testable — nonce dedup, pool mutual exclusion, ring
  prune, suppression transitions).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1/§4.2,
  `docs/adr/ADR-005` (zero-pyo3 + standalone-core), `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md`
  §3, `src/degenbot/calculations/evm_math.py` (the `next_base_fee` N1 leaf the block clock
  drives).
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` `Dispatcher` L579–L678 + the
  `PathSuppression` class L509–L578 (composed; delegated via `record_success`/
  `record_failure`/`is_suppressed`/`is_path_blocked`).
- The `active_tasks: set[asyncio.Task]` + `task.add_done_callback(discard)` Python pattern
  maps to a tokio `JoinSet` (or `task::AbortHandle` set). The `current_block_ref:
  list[int]` single-element mutable-by-reference maps to `Arc<Mutex<u64>>` (read by monitor
  tasks across the consumer/monitor boundary without a per-access lock in Python — Rust
  uses the `Mutex`). The `pending_nonces` `claim_nonce(start)` uses `itertools.count(start)`
  scanning for the first non-pending nonce — Rust: same linear scan over a `HashSet`.
- Crate placement: recommended `degenbot-submission` core crate (confirm with `t-6486`).
  `PathSuppression` is OWNED by the Simulation epic `5LLJHX` D-child (`5FB5MW`) per the
  4JGPDW scope — but `PathSuppression` is COMPOSED into `Dispatcher` here. **Flag:** if
  `5FB5MW` owns `PathSuppression`, this child REFERENCES its struct (compose, no hard
  edge); coordinate with the Simulation epic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `pub struct Dispatcher { pending_nonces, pending_pools, active_tasks
  (JoinSet), current_block (Arc<Mutex<u64>>), block_times, block_priority_fees,
  path_suppression }` with `claim_nonce`/`release_nonce`/`reserve_pools`/`release_pools`/
  `is_path_blocked`/`release_tx`/`track_task`/`advance_block`/`current_block`/
  `record_block_time`/`record_priority_fees`/`latest_priority_fees` + the `for_block`
  constructor + `PathSuppression` delegation.
- `pending_nonces` claim scans from `start` for the first non-member (matches the Python
  linear scan); `block_priority_fees` prunes to `FEE_HISTORY_WINDOW` on insert (pops the
  min key); `active_tasks` auto-discards on task completion (tokio `JoinSet`/abort-handle).
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests: nonce dedup/cap, pool mutual exclusion, ring prune,
  by-ref clock read across tasks.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- Parity check vs the Python `Dispatcher` behavior (§4.2 red-green).

## Non-goals
- `PathSuppression` internals — Simulation epic `5LLJHX` `5FB5MW` (REFERENCE/compose).
- The `next_base_fee` formula — N1 child (`JTLWA3`).
- The submit orchestration + sign + broadcast — N6/N4/N5 siblings.
- The `monitor_pending_transaction` lifecycle — N2 sibling.

## Dependencies
- REFERENCES `5FB5MW` (Simulation `PathSuppression`) for composition — no hard edge
  (compose the struct once it lands).

data.title: EIP-1559 transaction signing + fee finalization (alloy-signer-local LocalSigner owning operator key; TxEnvelope/Typed2718 type-2; maxFeePerGas 1.5x headroom; priority_fee CONSUMED from YL2MTH)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port **EIP-1559 transaction signing + fee finalization** to Rust: own the operator
  private key once via `alloy-signer-local::LocalSigner`; build the type-2 EIP-1559
  `TxEnvelope`/`Typed2718` transaction from `tx_params` (`to`/`data`=`execute()` calldata/
  `chainId`/`gas`/`nonce`/`value=0`/`accessList`); finalize `maxFeePerGas` =
  `int(1.5 * base_fee_next) + priority_fee` and `maxPriorityFeePerGas = priority_fee`
  (the `priority_fee` CONSUMED from `YL2MTH`); sign locally (ECDSA secp256k1) and return
  the raw signed `bytes`.

## Context
- Scope task: `P7AMWR` (epic `SHT6GE`), rows N4 + N5.
- Rubric dispositions: N4 `port-now` (hot per-tx; private-key handling must NEVER live in
  Python — security: today the key crosses into `eth_account` per-tx; `alloy-signer-local`
  owns the key once; `TxEnvelope`/`Typed2718` encoding is pure; property-testable
  signed-tx round-trip decode via alloy; §2.1 "I/O shape?" = crypto, no network;
  "type shape" = bytes). N5 `port-now` (pure integer fee arithmetic over `base_fee_next`
  (N1) + `priority_fee` from `YL2MTH`; the `1.5x` float→int headroom preserves the same
  float→int truncate convention as `_compute_priority_fee` — document the float boundary).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1/§4.2,
  `docs/adr/ADR-005` (zero-pyo3 + standalone-core + the security seam),
  `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md` §3.
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` L2623–L2640 —
  `tx_params["maxPriorityFeePerGas"] = priority_fee`;
  `tx_params["maxFeePerGas"] = int(1.5 * base_fee_next) + priority_fee`;
  `eth_account.Account.sign_transaction(transaction_dict=tx_params,
  private_key=operator_private_key).raw_transaction`. The fee constants
  (`TARGET_PROFIT_RATIO`/`AGE_DECAY_CONSTANT`/`MIN_PRIORITY_FEE_PERCENTILE`/
  `MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_PERCENTILE`) live in `_compute_priority_fee` (`YL2MTH`, Simulation).
- **Cross-epic (REFERENCE, no hard edge per orchestrator ruling Q2):** the
  `priority_fee` is CONSUMED from `YL2MTH`'s `_compute_priority_fee` via the `tx_params`
  the Simulation leaf returns. Submission does NOT sequence-depend on `YL2MTH`; it reads
  the already-computed fee off `tx_params`.
- Signing is EXPLICITLY carved out of `ZUZANP` (RPC epic `ZUZANP` body: "Signing —
  Transaction-submission epic (SHT6GE)"). `ZUZANP` owns only the byte-broadcast
  `eth_sendRawTransaction` (`bytes → TxHash`); this child owns the SIGNING that produces
  those bytes. `degenbot-rpc` has NO signing code today (`rg signer` empty in cores).
- Crate placement: recommended `degenbot-submission` core crate (deps `alloy` +
  `alloy-signer-local` + `degenbot-rpc` + `degenbot-core` + `degenbot-abi`/`degenbot-executor`
  for the `execute()` calldata EIP-2718 typing); PyO3 wrapper in
  `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/submission/`. **Confirm with `t-6486`.**

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `pub struct TxSigner { signer: LocalSigner<...>, chain_id: u64 }` holding the
  operator key ONCE (constructed from a Python-provided key bytes/hex via the PyO3
  wrapper — the key never round-trips back to Python per-tx).
- `pub fn finalize_fees(tx_params, base_fee_next, priority_fee) -> ()` setting
  `max_fee_per_gas = (1.5 * base_fee_next as f64) as u128 + priority_fee` (preserve the
  float→int truncate) + `max_priority_fee_per_gas = priority_fee`.
- `pub async fn sign_eip1559(tx_params) -> Bytes` building the `TxEnvelope` (type-2
  EIP-1559 fields: `maxFeePerGas`/`maxPriorityFeePerGas`/`chainId`/`accessList`/`nonce`/
  `gas`/`to`/`value=0`/`data`) + signing via the `LocalSigner`; returns the raw signed
  bytes ready for `eth_sendRawTransaction`.
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests: signed-tx round-trip decode via alloy's `TxEnvelope::decode`
  vs the Python `eth_account.sign_transaction` output over a fixture corpus (same
  `tx_params` + key → identical raw signed bytes); `proptest` for the fee-finalization
  arithmetic.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- `just test-rust-python` once the cutover wires the example.
- Byte-for-byte parity vs `eth_account.Account.sign_transaction(...).raw_transaction`
  (§4.2 red-green).

## Non-goals
- The `eth_sendRawTransaction` broadcast (`bytes → TxHash`) — `ZUZANP` (cross-epic D3DIPE)
  for the typed surface; the N6 child CONSUMES it.
- `next_base_fee` — N1 child (`JTLWA3`).
- `_compute_priority_fee` (the `priority_fee` value) — Simulation `YL2MTH` (REFERENCE,
  consume off `tx_params`).
- The submit orchestration (claim nonce → finalize → re-compute access list → sign →
  broadcast → monitor) — N6 sibling.
- The private-key CONFIG load — stays Python (S1; the driver loads the key and hands it to
  the Rust signer ONCE).

## Dependencies
- None hard (the `priority_fee` is consumed off `tx_params`, not hard-edged to `YL2MTH`).
- REFERENCES `JTLWA3` (N1) for `base_fee_next` if the signer leaf computes the headroom
  itself; otherwise the caller passes `base_fee_next` in (consume, no edge).

data.title: SubmittedTx + monitor_pending_transaction confirmation/expiry lifecycle (receipt poll, BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES void, nonce+pool release on confirm/expire)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port `SubmittedTx` + `monitor_pending_transaction` — the pending-tx confirmation/expiry
  lifecycle — to Rust: a typed `SubmittedTx { tx_hash: B256, nonce: u64, pools: HashSet,
  submission_block: u64 }` + an async loop that polls `get_transaction_receipt` (≈1s sleep
  between polls); on receipt (`confirmed`) → release nonce + pools; on
  `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES` blocks without inclusion → void the nonce, release pools,
  return. Reads `dispatcher.current_block` by-reference.

## Context
- Scope task: `P7AMWR` (epic `SHT6GE`), row N2.
- Rubric disposition: `port-now` (pure lifecycle state machine over
  `get_transaction_receipt` (I3) + `dispatcher.current_block` + the
  `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES` constant; property-testable — confirm/expiry transitions;
  the §2.1 "GIL?" win is modest — 1s sleep poll — but the lifecycle/control-flow belongs
  in Rust alongside the nonce owner N3; the monitor is spawned as a tokio task by the N6
  submit orchestration).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1/§4.2,
  `docs/adr/ADR-005` (zero-pyo3 + standalone-core), `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md`
  §3.
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` `SubmittedTx` L1617–L1622 +
  `monitor_pending_transaction` L1624–L1652. `TransactionNotFound` exception from web3.py's
  `get_transaction_receipt` → "not yet included" branch (Rust: the receipt leaf returns
  `Option`/`None` for not-found).
- The `dispatcher.current_block` read-by-reference: Python uses a single-element list
  (`current_block_ref[0]`) so monitor tasks read the current block across the
  consumer/monitor boundary without a lock; Rust uses `Arc<Mutex<u64>>` (or
  `Arc<AtomicU64>`) — read with a single cheap load.
- `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES = 5` (network constant; submit reveals `5` for mainnet).
- Crate placement: recommended `degenbot-submission` core crate (confirm with `t-6486`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `pub struct SubmittedTx { tx_hash: B256, nonce: u64, pools: HashSet<String>,
  submission_block: u64 }` + `pub async fn monitor_pending_transaction(tx, provider,
  dispatcher, blocks_before_nonce_expires: u64) -> MonitorOutcome` returning
  `Confirmed`/`Expired(blocks_waited)`.
- Polls every ~1s (`tokio::time::sleep`); on receipt-found → `Confirmed` + release nonce
  + pools via `dispatcher.release_tx`; on `blocks_waited >
  blocks_before_nonce_expires` → `Expired` + release_tx (void nonce) + return.
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests: confirm-on-first-poll, expire-after-threshold,
  release-on-both-paths; mock the receipt provider.
- Spawns as a tokio task tracked by `Dispatcher::track_task` (N3 `active_tasks` JoinSet).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- `just test-rust-python` once the cutover wires the example.
- Parity check vs the Python `monitor_pending_transaction` confirm/expire behavior
  (§4.2 red-green).

## Non-goals
- `get_transaction_receipt` typed RPC — `degenbot-rpc::AlloyProvider::get_transaction_receipt`
  L688 (I3, EXISTS; the confirmation-status decode is the partial surface).
- `Dispatcher` nonce/pool state — N3 child (`M756BN`) (CONSUME `release_tx`/`current_block`).
- The submit orchestration that SPAWNS the monitor — N6 sibling.

## Dependencies
- Depends on N3 `M756BN` (the `Dispatcher` it calls `release_tx`/reads `current_block` on).
- CONSUMES `get_transaction_receipt` (C1/I3, EXISTS in `degenbot-rpc`) — no new RPC leaf.

data.title: dispatch_profitable_results submit orchestration + eth_sendRawTransaction broadcast + eth_feeHistory percentile fetch (typed consumer of ZUZANP; interim make_request fallback, dry_run/inject_code guards)
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the **`dispatch_profitable_results` submit orchestration** + the
  **`eth_sendRawTransaction` broadcast** + the **`eth_feeHistory` percentile fetch** to
  Rust: sort candidates by engine profit descending; mutual-exclusivity check
  (`is_path_blocked` against pending+committed pools); `INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE`/`dry_run`
  safety-guard skips live submission (CONFIG policy gate, S3 stays-python); claim nonce
  (N3) → finalize fees (N5) → re-compute access list (C5/`PGA5S3`) → sign (N4) →
  broadcast via `eth_sendRawTransaction` (I1/`ZUZANP`) → reserve pools (N3) → spawn the
  monitor task (N2). Plus the `eth_feeHistory` percentile fetch feeding the `Dispatcher`
  `block_priority_fees` ring.

## Context
- Scope task: `P7AMWR` (epic `SHT6GE`), rows N6 + I1 + I2.
- Rubric dispositions: N6 `port-now` (pure orchestration over leaves N3/N4/N5/N2 + C5 +
  I1; the §2.1 "GIL?" win — owning the sign+broadcast slice in Rust releases the GIL
  across the async broadcast; the sort + mutual-exclusivity is pure). I1 `partial`
  (`eth_sendRawTransaction` — untyped `make_request` EXISTS in `degenbot-rpc` L809 so
  broadcast CAN route through Rust today; the TYPED `bytes → TxHash` is `ZUZANP`
  cross-epic D3DIPE). I2 `partial` (`eth_feeHistory` — same shape; typed consumer `ZUZANP`).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §3.1/§3.2 (PyO3)
  /§4.2 (parity), `docs/adr/ADR-005` (zero-pyo3 + standalone-core),
  `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md` §3.
- Python oracle: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` `dispatch_profitable_results`
  submit tail L2608–L2660 (the `dry_run` guard L2608, `INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE` guard L2612,
  claim nonce L2622, finalize fees L2623–L2625, re-compute access list L2627–L2630,
  sign+broadcast L2636–L2640, reserve pools L2648, spawn monitor L2650–L2656) + the
  `_apply_block_if_ready` `feeHistory` fetch L2832–L2841.
- **Cross-epic (hard edge, per orchestrator ruling Q1):** `ZUZANP` (D3DIPE) types exactly
  `eth_sendRawTransaction` + `eth_feeHistory` — KEEP hard `ZUZANP`→this-child edge; interim
  untyped `make_request` (L809) fallback ONLY if `ZUZANP` blocked (§4.2 wait-for-typed
  default).
- **Cross-epic (REFERENCE, no hard edge):** the `tx_params` (+ `priority_fee`) CONSUMED
  from `YL2MTH` (Simulation); the access-list re-computation CONSUMED from `PGA5S3`
  (Simulation `eth_createAccessList`). Per orchestrator ruling Q2, Submission does NOT
  sequence-depend on `YL2MTH`.
- Crate placement: recommended `degenbot-submission` core crate (confirm with `t-6486`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure-Rust `async fn dispatch_and_submit(gas_profitable: Vec<SimResult>, dispatcher,
  provider, signer, base_fee_next, current_block, inject_code: bool, dry_run: bool) ->
  SubmitOutcome` orchestrating: sort by engine profit desc → for each: mutual-exclusivity
  guard → `dry_run`/`inject_code` guard (RETURN a typed Skip reason, don't submit) → claim
  nonce (`M756BN`) → finalize fees (`G6DNW4`) → re-compute access list via
  `eth_createAccessList` → sign (`G6DNW4`) → broadcast via `eth_sendRawTransaction`
  (`ZUZANP` typed; interim `make_request` untyped) → `reserve_pools` → spawn
  `monitor_pending_transaction` (`HF2R2E`) tracked by `Dispatcher::track_task`.
- `async fn fetch_fee_history(provider, block_number, percentiles) -> FeeHistory` typed
  consumer of `eth_feeHistory` (`ZUZANP` typed; interim `make_request`) feeding
  `Dispatcher::record_priority_fees`.
- `dry_run`/`inject_code` are passed as `bool` args from the Python driver (S3 policy
  gate) — the leaf exposes them as config, NOT as Python policy.
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity tests: submit order (profit-desc), mutual-exclusivity skip,
  `dry_run`/`inject_code` skip, nonce-fee-access-sign-broadcast sequence; mock the
  provider + signer.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.
- `just test-rust-python` once the cutover wires the example.
- Parity check vs the Python `dispatch_profitable_results` submit tail (§4.2 red-green).

## Non-goals
- Signing + fee finalization — N4/N5 child (`G6DNW4`).
- `Dispatcher` coordination — N3 child (`M756BN`).
- `monitor_pending_transaction` lifecycle — N2 child (`HF2R2E`).
- `_compute_priority_fee` (the `priority_fee` value) — Simulation `YL2MTH` (consume off
  `tx_params`, reference not hard-edge).
- `eth_simulateV1`/`eth_createAccessList` typed RPC — `ZUZANP` (this child CONSUMES
  `eth_createAccessList` + `eth_sendRawTransaction` + `eth_feeHistory`).
- The `dry_run`/`INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE` policy (the live-submission skip as a POLICY) —
  stays Python (S3); the leaf takes them as bool config.
- The `next_base_fee` formula — N1 child (`JTLWA3`).

## Dependencies
- Depends on N3 `M756BN` (Dispatcher), N4/N5 `G6DNW4` (sign+fee), N2 `HF2R2E` (monitor).
- Hard edge: `ZUZANP` (cross-epic D3DIPE, typed `eth_sendRawTransaction` +
  `eth_feeHistory` — interim untyped `make_request` fallback ONLY if blocked).
- REFERENCE (no hard edge): `YL2MTH` (Simulation, `tx_params`+`priority_fee`) +
  `PGA5S3` (Simulation, `eth_createAccessList`).

data.title: Extend Rust PoolStateSubscriber/LogDispatcher with a PySubscriberAdapter seam; retire parallel Python PublisherMixin dispatch on Rust-owned pools
data.body:
## Goal
- Extend the existing Rust pub/sub **mechanism** (`degenbot-bot`'s `PoolStateSubscriber` trait + `LogDispatcher::{subscribe,notify,dispatch}` + the `Weak<dyn PoolStateSubscriber>` fan-out + `EngineSubscriber`) to be the single notification path for ALL Rust-owned state changes — including Python-driven state mutations that today go through the parallel Python `PublisherMixin._notify_subscribers` — by exposing a PyO3 seam that lets a `#[pyclass]` Python `Subscriber` register as a `PoolStateSubscriber` (or a new `dyn` adapter) so Rust-owned `BotState` mutations notify Rust AND Python subscribers through one mechanism. Retire the parallel Python `PublisherMixin` dispatch on pool/token types once their state is Rust-owned.

## Context
- Scope task: `I7KVKM` (Epic `2K2JP4`). Rubric disposition: **port-now** (the mechanism) / **stays-python** (the consumers).
- §2.1 criteria (the mechanism): type=pure (pool_id u64 / message tag); I/O=none (in-process `Weak` fan-out); **hot path** (fires per decoded log in the pump — `LogDispatcher::dispatch` is the slice-4 decode→apply→notify spine); GIL: the Rust path is GIL-free (engine dirty-mark under `parking_lot::Mutex`, no Python). §2.3 duplication smell **CONFIRMED + already partially resolved**: Rust own s a complete pub/sub mechanism (`PoolStateSubscriber` trait + `LogDispatcher` `Weak`-fan-out + `EngineSubscriber` + `DrainSink::on_drain`/`on_send`/`notify_block`) running on `BotState`; Python has a PARALLEL mechanism (`Publisher`/`Subscriber`/`PublisherMixin._notify_subscribers` over a `WeakSet` of Python subscribers) on the Python pool classes (`UniswapV2/3/4Pool`, `AerodromeV2Pool`, `BalancerV2Pool`, `BalancerV2StablePool`, `CurveStableswapPool`) each calling `self._notify_subscribers(message=...PoolStateUpdated(self.state))`. The two aren't bridged: a Python subscriber can't receive Rust `BotState` notifications and vice-versa.
- This is the **IN-FIGHT** convergence task: extend the Rust mechanism with a "Python subscriber adapter" (a `#[pyclass]` implementing `PoolStateSubscriber` that holds a `Py<PyAny>` callback / Python `Subscriber` and calls it under `py.detach()`/with the GIL) so Python consumers can subscribe to Rust-owned state notifications through the SAME `LogDispatcher` path the `EngineSubscriber` uses. Then retire `PublisherMixin._notify_subscribers` on pool classes whose state is Rust-owned.
- Deps: NONE cross-epic. The Rust mechanism (`degenbot-bot`) is already landed (this is extending it). NO `SLHSM4` edge (pub/sub is in-process, not DB). NO `BotState` edge issue — `BotState` + `LogDispatcher` are co-located in `degenbot-bot`, already Rust-owned (a "done" reference, not a dep to wire).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A `#[pyclass]` `PySubscriberAdapter` (or `#[pyfunction] subscribe_to_pool(bot, pool_id, py_callback)`) in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/` implementing `degenbot_bot::bot_core::log_dispatcher::PoolStateSubscriber`, holding a `Py<PyAny>` (the Python `Subscriber` or callback) — registered with `LogDispatcher::subscribe(pool_id, adapter.weak_handle())`. On `on_pool_state_updated`, it re-acquires the GIL and invokes the Python `notify` (or callback). Registered in `c_api.rs`.
- The Python `Publisher`/`Subscriber`/`PublisherMixin` in `src/degenbot/types/concrete.py` become thin delegating shells OR are retired for pool/token types whose state is Rust-owned: the pool's `_notify_subscribers(message=PoolStateUpdated(...))` bodies deleted; state-change notifications route through the Rust `LogDispatcher` (which already fires on `dispatch`→`apply`→`notify`). Python `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` on a pool delegate to the Rust seam (registering a `PySubscriberAdapter`).
- A `PoolStateMessage`/`...PoolStateUpdated` equivalent surfaced to Python subscribers (the adapter builds the message object Python expects, or passes a `(publisher_handle, state)` tuple matching the `Subscriber.notify(publisher, message)` protocol).
- Parity (§4.2): a Python `FakeSubscriber` (`tests/fakes/subscribers.py`) registered against a Rust-owned pool receives the same notifications (same pool, same state-order) as the prior Python path. Keep the Python path as oracle until green, then retire per §4.3.
- Pyo3-free cores enforced (`just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` — the adapter lives in `degenbot-python` only; `PoolStateSubscriber`/`LogDispatcher` stay pyo3-free).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just test-python` (`tests/types/test_publisher_mixin.py`, `tests/types/test_pool_protocols.py`, `tests/fakes/subscribers.py` consumers), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- Migrating Python **consumer/subscriber** orchestration (the `engine_registry`/`build_paths`/CLI update loops that subscribe to drive update cycles) — stays-python (sibling task, consumer concerns).
- The `EngineSubscriber` + `DrainSink` (on_drain/on_send/notify_block) Rust path — already landed; this task only adds the Python-bridge adapter, doesn't touch the engine's own wiring.
- `TextMessage` (the generic text publisher message) — stays Python (a Python-only convenience message type with no Rust-state equivalent); only `PoolStateMessage`/`PoolStateUpdated` bridges.
- RPC WebSocket `eth_subscribe`/`subscribe_blocks`/`subscribe_logs` (in `bot.py`/`engine_registry`) — that's RPC pub-sub, a different concern (Epic for `degenbot-rpc`), not this in-process message mechanism.

data.title: Route Python pub/sub consumers (engine_registry/CLI/test fakes) through the PySubscriberAdapter seam; consumer reaction bodies stay Python
data.body:
## Goal
- Convert the Python **pub/sub consumers** (classes/functions that subscribe to a `Publisher` to drive an update loop) into delegating shells that subscribe through the Rust `PoolStateSubscriber` seam (sibling mechanism task) instead of the Python `PublisherMixin`. These are the Python-orchestration consumers: the `FakeSubscriber` test helper pattern, the `engine_registry` subscribe-to-engine wiring, and any pool-state-driven update hooks. They stay **Python** (orchestration), but their *subscription* routes through Rust.

## Context
- Scope task: `I7KVKM` (Epic `2K2JP4`). Rubric disposition: **stays-python** (the consumers are orchestration/drivers), with their subscription *call* routed through the sibling Rust seam.
- §2.1 "Keep in Python" criteria: these consumers orchestrate update loops (subscribe → react → drive further Python I/O) — orchestration is a shell concern; the *mechanism* they use is the Rust one (sibling task). eco: they couple to Python async/CLI orchestration.
- KEY DISTINCTION (orchestrator's): MECHANISM = the dispatch/listener infra (sibling task, `port-now`). CONSUMERS = these orchestration subscribers (`stays-python`, this task routes their subscribe call only).
- Deps: sibling mechanism task (the `PySubscriberAdapter` / `subscribe_to_pool` seam they register through).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The Python consumer subscribe callsites (e.g. `engine_registry` WS subscribe, CLI update-loop subscriptions, `FakeSubscriber.subscribe` in tests) call the Rust seam (`PySubscriberAdapter`) when subscribing to a Rust-owned pool/token, instead of `Publisher.subscribe`.
- The consumer *reaction* bodies (what `notify` does — drive an update, record for assertion, etc.) stay Python and unchanged.
- `tests/fakes/subscribers.py::FakeSubscriber` updated to subscribe via the Rust seam when targeting a Rust-owned publisher (or kept dual-mode for Python-only publishers); `tests/types/test_publisher_mixin.py` + `test_pool_protocols.py` parity preserved.
- Parity (§4.2): consumers receive notifications in the same order/shape via the Rust seam as via the prior Python path.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (`tests/types/*`, `tests/fakes/`, `tests/arbitrage/*` consumer suites), `just test-rust-python`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- The Rust pub/sub mechanism + `PySubscriberAdapter` (sibling task).
- The RPC WebSocket `eth_subscribe` subscribe loops (`engine_registry.subscribe`, `bot.py subscribe_blocks/logs`) — separate RPC concern.
- Porting consumer orchestration logic itself to Rust (it stays Python by disposition).

## Goal
- Identify the full scope of the **Transaction submission → Rust core** migration so
  subsequent child tasks decompose into `done` / `partial` / `port-now` / `stays-python`
  dispositions per the ADR-005 transition rubric
  (`docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.1 criteria / §2.2 dispositions /
  §2.3 smells / §3 cutover discipline / §4 red-green parity + retirement).

## Context (responsibility boundary)
- The **Transaction submission** responsibility = everything between "profitable
  `tx_params` ready" (output of the Simulation epic `5LLJHX` `YL2MTH`) and "signed raw tx
  broadcast + confirmation/receipt handled". It: claims a nonce (source-of-truth from
  `eth_getTransactionCount`), finalizes EIP-1559 fee fields (`maxFeePerGas` /
  `maxPriorityFeePerGas` — the priority fee is CONSUMED from `YL2MTH`/`_compute_priority_fee`,
  REFERENCE not hard-edge), re-computes the EIP-2930 access list with the updated
  nonce/fees, signs the typed-2 transaction locally (`eth_account.sign_transaction`),
  broadcasts via `eth_sendRawTransaction`, and monitors the pending tx until confirmation
  or expiry (`get_transaction_receipt` polled; nonce voided + pools released on expiry).
- Today this lives ENTIRELY in Python: `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`
  (`dispatch_profitable_results`'s submit block L2608–L2660, `monitor_pending_transaction`
  L1624–L1652, `SubmittedTx` L1617, `Dispatcher` nonce/pool/task coordination L579–L678,
  `_apply_block_if_ready` block-clock + `feeHistory` + `next_base_fee` orchestration
  L2801–L2857, the `main()` start-phase `operator_nonce` + `base_fee_next` fetches
  L2884/L2920–L2921) + `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py` + `src/degenbot/calculations/evm_math.py`
  (`next_base_fee` L17–L73, the EIP-1559 base-fee formula). The Rust `degenbot-rpc` crate
  owns the transport primitives (`get_transaction_count` L776, `estimate_gas` L615,
  `get_transaction` L654, `get_transaction_receipt` L688, the untyped `make_request`
  L809), but ZERO signing / `TxEnvelope` construction / private-key handling / nonce
  coordination / tx-confirmation lifecycle exists in any Rust crate.
- Canonical reading order applied: `AGENTS.md` (Architectural Vision → "the transaction
  submission" is on the migration path; "Rust is the engine, Python is the cockpit") →
  `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §2.1/§2.2 → `docs/adr/ADR-005`
  (standalone-core + zero-`pyo3`-in-cores) → `docs/architecture/rust-owned-bot.md` §17
  (known-limitation: "transaction submission — today Python via `examples/`; on the
  migration path").
- Baseline gate: `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` PASS (untouched by scoping).
- **Crate placement (recommended):** a new core crate `degenbot-submission` (pyo3-free;
  deps `alloy` + `degenbot-rpc` + `degenbot-core` + `degenbot-abi` + `degenbot-executor`
  for the `execute()` calldata EIP-2718 typing), PyO3 wrappers in
  `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/submission/`. Mirrors the `degenbot-executor`/
  `degenbot-simulation` precedent; keeps `degenbot-bot` I/O-free per ADR-001 / ADR-003.
  Signing uses `alloy-signer-local` (the `LocalSigner` carrying the operator private key)
  — confirmed no signing code exists in `degenbot-rpc` today (`rg signer` empty); the
  signer lives in the new submission crate. **Confirm with `t-6486`** (consistent with
  the WWC4DL/`5LLJHX` crate decisions).

## Scope table

### COMPLETED — Rust-owned (do NOT redo)

| # | Row | Rust source | Python consumer | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|-----|-------------|-----------------|-------------|-----------|
| C1 | `AlloyProvider::get_transaction_count` (nonce source-of-truth via `eth_getTransactionCount`, pending/latest selectable) | `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/provider.rs` L776–L806 | python `main()` L2884 `async_w3.eth.get_transaction_count` | `done` | Typed nonce RPC leaf exists with retry/backoff; the submission leaf CONSUMES it. |
| C2 | `AlloyProvider::estimate_gas` + `eth_call` + `get_block` + `get_balance`/`get_code`/`get_storage_at` | `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/provider.rs` L570–L750, L491 | python dispatch (gas/fee/access list pre-call) | `done` | Transport-primitive precedent; the typed `eth_sendRawTransaction`/`eth_feeHistory` are `ZUZANP` (see I1/I3). |
| C3 | Typed RPC leaves + the untyped `make_request` escape hatch (`method + serde_json::Value → Value`, retry/backoff) | `rust/crates/degenbot-rpc/src/provider.rs` L809–L829 | the broadcast + receipt-poll callsites route here (interim-untyped for sendRaw) | `done` (leaf exists) | The untyped escape hatch the submission broadcast (I2/I3) routes through UNTIL `ZUZANP` types `eth_sendRawTransaction`. Retry/backoff already owned in Rust. |
| C4 | Profitable `tx_params` (to/`execute()` calldata/type=2/gas accessList placeholders; `priority_fee`+`gas_used`+`net_profit` from the sim) | produced by Simulation epic `5LLJHX` `YL2MTH` (`simulate_one` returns `tx_params`) | consumed at L2618 | `done` (reference) | The submission leaf's INPUT is already Rust-owned; per orchestrator ruling, REFERENCE `YL2MTH`'s fee — CONSUME `tx_params`, NO hard-edge. |
| C5 | The EIP-2930 access list computed during simulation (re-computed post-nonce/fee update via the B-leaf `eth_createAccessList`) | Simulation `PGA5S3` + RPC `ZUZANP` | python L2627–L2630 re-computes | `done` (reference) | CONSUMED from `PGA5S3`/`ZUZANP`; the re-computation is the same leaf called twice. Reference, do not re-scope. |

### IN-FIGHT — partially routed; Python still the authority for some callsites

| # | Row | Python source | Rust counterpart | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------------|-------------|------------------|
| I1 | `eth_sendRawTransaction` broadcast | python L2636–L2640 (`async_w3.eth.send_raw_transaction(...)`) | `degenbot-rpc::AlloyProvider::make_request("eth_sendRawTransaction", …)` (untyped, EXISTS); typed `eth_sendRawTransaction` (`bytes → TxHash`) = `ZUZANP` (NOT-STARTED, cross-epic D3DIPE) | `partial` | The untyped escape hatch EXISTS — broadcast CAN route through Rust today untyped; the TYPED request/response is `ZUZANP` (carves out "Signing — SHT6GE"; owns only the byte-broadcast `bytes → TxHash`). Cross-epic dep; interim-untyped fallback ONLY if `ZUZANP` blocked (per orchestrator ruling Q1). |
| I2 | `eth_feeHistory` percentile fetch (feeds `_compute_priority_fee` + `Dispatcher.record_priority_fees`) | python L2832–L2841 (`async_w3.eth.fee_history`) | `make_request("eth_feeHistory", …)` untyped EXISTS; typed = `ZUZANP` | `partial` | Same shape as I1 — untyped available; typed consumer `ZUZANP`. The percentile extraction + the `Dispatcher` dict shape is pure (rows N1/N3). Cross-epic dep. |
| I3 | `eth_getTransactionReceipt` poll (tx confirmation) | python L1639 (`async_w3.eth.get_transaction_receipt(tx.tx_hash)`) | `degenbot-rpc::AlloyProvider::get_transaction_receipt` L688 (TYPED, EXISTS — returns `serde_json::Value`) | `done`-leaning→`partial` | The typed receipt leaf EXISTS (`get_transaction_receipt` L688). It returns `serde_json::Value` not a typed receipt struct, so the CONFIRMATION-status decode (status field) is the partial surface. The poll loop itself is N2/port-now. |

### NOT STARTED — no Rust counterpart; per rubric belongs in Rust

| # | Row | Python source | Rust counterpart | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------------|-------------|------------------|
| N1 | `next_base_fee` (pure EIP-1559 base-fee formula from `parent_base_fee`/`gas_used`/`gas_limit` + `elasticity_multiplier`/`base_fee_max_change_denominator`/`min_base_fee`) | `src/degenbot/calculations/evm_math.py` L17–L73; called L2825/L2920 | none | `port-now` | Pure integer EVM math; hot per-block; no I/O; no float; property-testable (round-trip, target-bound, min clamp). Standalone-Rust-usable — belongs in a new `degenbot-evm-math` core crate (the `next_base_fee` precedent mirrors `cl_msb`/`cl_lsb` already in `degenbot-core/src/`). The `min_base_fee` arg supports non-Ethereum EIP-1559 chains (linea). **Cross-epic:** consumed by both Submission (fee finalization) AND Simulation (`base_fee_next` for net-profit). |
| N2 | `SubmittedTx` + `monitor_pending_transaction` async confirmation loop (poll receipt each second; on confirmed → release nonce+pools; on `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES` blocks without inclusion → void nonce, release pools; `dispatcher.current_block` read-by-reference) | python L1617–L1652 | none | `port-now` | Pure lifecycle state machine over `get_transaction_receipt` (I3) + `dispatcher.current_block` + `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES`; the §2.1 "GIL?" win is modest (1s sleep poll) but the lifecycle/control-flow belongs in Rust alongside the nonce owner. Property-testable (confirm/expiry transitions). |
| N3 | `Dispatcher` nonce/pool/task coordination (`claim_nonce`/`release_nonce`/`reserve_pools`/`release_pools`/`is_path_blocked`/`track_task` + `active_tasks` auto-discard; `pending_nonces: HashSet`; `pending_pools: HashSet`; `current_block_ref` by-ref read; `record_block_time`/`record_priority_fees`/`latest_priority_fees` ring-buffer prune) | python L579–L678 | none | `port-now` | Pure coordination state (`HashMap`/`HashSet` + a single-element `Arc<Mutex<u64>>` for the by-ref block clock); hot per-tx; GIL-held today across claim/release; property-testable (nonce dedup, pool mutual exclusion, ring prune). The `active_tasks:auto-discard` is a Python-asyncio shape that maps to a tokio `JoinSet`. |
| N4 | EIP-1559 transaction signing (`eth_account.Account.sign_transaction(transaction_dict, private_key) → raw_transaction bytes`; local ECDSA secp256k1 signing; type-2 EIP-1559 fields: `maxFeePerGas`/`maxPriorityFeePerGas`/`chainId`/`accessList`/`nonce`/`gas`/`to`/`value`/`data`) | python L2637–L2640 | none (signing explicitly carved out of `ZUZANP` — "Signing — Transaction-submission epic (SHT6GE)") | `port-now` | Hot per-tx; private-key handling must NEVER live in Python (security: the key currently crosses into `eth_account` per-tx). `alloy-signer-local::LocalSigner` owns the key once; `TxEnvelope` + `Typed2718` encoding is pure; property-testable (signed-tx round-trip decode via alloy). The §2.1 "I/O shape?" is crypto (no network) + "type shape" is bytes. This is the canonical SHT6GE leaf. |
| N5 | EIP-1559 fee finalization (`maxFeePerGas = int(1.5 * base_fee_next) + priority_fee`; `maxPriorityFeePerGas = priority_fee` from `YL2MTH`; the `1.5x` base-fee headroom factor) | python L2623–L2625 | none | `port-now` | Pure integer fee arithmetic over `base_fee_next` (N1) + `priority_fee` (CONSUMED from `YL2MTH` — REFERENCE); the `1.5x` float→int headroom preserves the same float→int truncate convention as `_compute_priority_fee` (document the float boundary). Small — folds with N4/N6. |
| N6 | `dispatch_profitable_results` submit orchestration (sort by engine profit descending; mutual-exclusivity check `is_path_blocked` against pending+committed pools; `INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE` safety guard skips live submission; `dry_run` guard; DRY_RUN path logs-only; claim nonce → finalize fees → re-compute access list (C5) → sign (N4) → broadcast (I1) → reserve pools → spawn monitor (N2)) | python `dispatch_profitable_results` submit tail L2608–L2660 | none | `port-now` | Pure orchestration over leaves N3/N4/N5/C5/I1 + `dry_run` config branch; the §2.1 "GIL?" win is owning the sign+broadcast slice in Rust (releases the GIL across the async broadcast). The sort + mutual-exclusivity is pure. |

### `stays-python` — display/config/IO-shell (NOT a child)

| # | Row | Python source | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|-----|---------------|-------------|-----------|
| S1 | `main()` start-phase fetches (`operator_nonce` via `get_transaction_count`; initial `base_fee_next` via `next_base_fee` over the latest block); `DegenbotConfig`/`operator_private_key` config load; `dotenv_values("examples/mainmain.env")` | `stays-python` | Config bootstrap + secret loading (per "Python is the cockpit" + §2.1 "I/O shape": the private key is loaded by the Python driver and handed to the Rust signer ONCE). No per-tx logic. |
| S2 | `[submit]`/`[dispatch]` logging (submit hash, nonce, skip reasons, voided-nonce, confirmed-tx) | `stays-python` | Display/orchestration; infrequent (per-submit); Python-ecosystem (logging). The lifecycle RESULTS surface as typed structs the Python companion renders. |
| S3 | `DRY_RUN` / `INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE` safety-guard policy (the live-submission skip + the reason log) | `stays-python` (config policy) | Policy gates read from env/config; the GATE check is a thin Python branch over a bool. The submission leaf exposes `dry_run`/`inject_code` as args (pure bool config); the POLICY stays Python. |

## Child-task split (port-now / partial rows → implementation tasks)

- **N1** → child: *`next_base_fee` EIP-1559 base-fee math (core leaf — new `degenbot-evm-math` crate OR `degenbot-core`)*. CONSUMED by Submission (N5/N6) AND Simulation (`base_fee_next` net-profit). Notes a cross-epic REFERENCE for `5LLJHX` (simulation also reads `base_fee_next`); the orchestrator ruled reference-not-hard-edge for fees, so N1 is owned here and Simulation references it.
- **N3** → child: *`Dispatcher` nonce/pool/task coordination state (nonce claim/release, pool mutual exclusion, `active_tasks` JoinSet, `current_block_ref` by-ref clock, `block_priority_fees` ring prune)*.
- **N4 + N5** → child: *EIP-1559 transaction signing + fee finalization (`alloy-signer-local::LocalSigner` owning the operator key; `TxEnvelope`/`Typed2718` encoding; `maxFeePerGas`/`maxPriorityFeePerGas` with the 1.5x base-fee headroom, priority fee CONSUMED from `YL2MTH`)*. Carves out the key-handling seam (security).
- **N2** → child: *`SubmittedTx` + `monitor_pending_transaction` confirmation/expiry lifecycle (receipt poll, `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES` void, nonce+pool release on confirm/expire)*. Depends on N3 + I3 (`get_transaction_receipt`).
- **N6 + I1 + I2** → child: *`dispatch_profitable_results` submit orchestration + `eth_sendRawTransaction` broadcast + `eth_feeHistory` percentile fetch (typed consumer of `ZUZANP`; interim untyped `make_request` fallback ONLY if `ZUZANP` blocked)*. Depends on N3/N4/N5/N2 + `ZUZANP` (cross-epic D3DIPE, hard edge per Q1 ruling) + `PGA5S3`/`YL2MTH` (REFERENCE, no hard edge).

`stays-python` rows (S1 config/secret bootstrap, S2 submit logging, S3 dry-run/inject policy gates) — NO child; flagged so the next sweep does not re-litigate. Reference rows (C1–C5) — provided by `degenbot-rpc` / Simulation `YL2MTH`/`PGA5S3` / `ZUZANP`; consumed not re-scoped.

## Open dependency / blocking questions

1. **`ZUZANP` (RPC epic D3DIPE) is the critical path for the N6 submit-orchestration child** (typed `eth_sendRawTransaction` + typed `eth_feeHistory`). Per orchestrator ruling Q1: KEEP hard `ZUZANP`→N6-child edge; interim-untyped `make_request` (L809) fallback ONLY if `ZUZANP` blocked (§4.2 wait-for-typed default). Cross-epic child edge: N6-child → `ZUZANP`.
2. **`YL2MTH` fee — REFERENCE not hard-edge** (per orchestrator ruling Q2). The N4/N5 child CONSUMES `tx_params` (incl. the `priority_fee` computed in `YL2MTH`); Submission does NOT sequence-depend on the `YL2MTH` fee leaf. Wired as a reference, NO `ergo sequence` edge.
3. **`PGA5S3` access-list re-computation — REFERENCE.** The N6 child re-computes the access list via the same `eth_createAccessList` leaf the Simulation `PGA5S3` exposes; CONSUME, no hard edge.
4. **Crate placement: `degenbot-submission`?** Recommended new core crate (mirrors `degenbot-executor`/`degenbot-simulation`; keeps `degenbot-bot` I/O-free per ADR-001/ADR-003). Signing uses `alloy-signer-local` — confirmed NO signing code in `degenbot-rpc` today (`rg signer` empty in cores). **Confirm with `t-6486`** — consistent with the WWC4DL/`5LLJHX` crate decisions; alternatively fold into `degenbot-rpc` (but that bloats the transport crate with signer+nonce+confirmation lifecycle). `next_base_fee` (N1) recommended for a `degenbot-evm-math` core crate OR `degenbot-core` (it's pure EVM math, not submission-specific — consumed by Simulation too).
5. **Private-key security boundary.** The Python driver loads the operator key (S1 stays-python) and hands it to the Rust `LocalSigner` ONCE; the key MUST NOT live in Python per-tx. The N4 child owns the signer lifecycle; flag the key-handling seam in the cutover.
6. **`result` field cosmetic.** `ergo --json set ... '{"state":"done","result":"docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md"}'` shows `result: None` on round-trip (known gotcha). The body carries the result pointer; the tree view shows done.
## Child-task IDs (real, ergo-generated)

| ID | Title | Purpose |
|----|-------|---------|
| `JTLWA3` | `next_base_fee` EIP-1559 base-fee math (core leaf) | Pure integer EIP-1559 formula (`degenbot-evm-math` OR `degenbot-core`); CONSUMED cross-epic by Simulation (`base_fee_next`). |
| `M756BN` | `Dispatcher` nonce/pool/task coordination | claim/release nonce, pool mutual exclusion, `active_tasks` JoinSet, `current_block` by-ref clock, `block_priority_fees` ring prune, delegates `PathSuppression` (REFERENCE `5FB5MW`). |
| `G6DNW4` | EIP-1559 signing + fee finalization | `alloy-signer-local::LocalSigner` owns operator key once; `TxEnvelope`/`Typed2718` type-2; `maxFeePerGas` 1.5x headroom; `priority_fee` CONSUMED from `YL2MTH` (reference, no hard edge). |
| `HF2R2E` | `SubmittedTx` + `monitor_pending_transaction` | Pending-tx confirmation/expiry lifecycle (receipt poll, `BLOCKS_BEFORE_NONCE_EXPIRES` void, nonce+pool release on confirm/expire). |
| `PLDP23` | `dispatch_profitable_results` submit orchestration + `eth_sendRawTransaction` + `eth_feeHistory` | Sort + mutual-exclusivity + `dry_run`/`inject_code` guards → claim nonce → finalize fees → re-compute access list → sign → broadcast → reserve pools → spawn monitor. Hard-edge on `ZUZANP`. |

`stays-python` rows (no child): S1 (`main()` nonce/base-fee start fetches + config/secret
bootstrap), S2 (submit/dispatch logging), S3 (`dry_run`/`INJECT_EXECUTOR_CODE` policy
gates — the leaf takes bool args; the POLICY stays Python). Reference rows (C1–C5):
`get_transaction_count`/`estimate_gas`/`get_transaction_receipt`/`make_request` in
`degenbot-rpc`; `tx_params`+`priority_fee` from Simulation `YL2MTH`; access-list re-compute
from Simulation `PGA5S3`; typed `eth_sendRawTransaction`/`eth_feeHistory` from `ZUZANP`
(hard edge to `PLDP23`).

## Dependency edges (ergo `sequence`)

```
CROSS-EPIC (D3DIPE → SHT6GE):   ZUZANP (typed sendRaw + feeHistory) ──► PLDP23 (N6)
                                  (HARD edge per Q1; interim make_request fallback ONLY if blocked)

CROSS-EPIC (REFERENCE, no edge): YL2MTH (Simulation, tx_params + priority_fee) ── consumed by G6DNW4
                                 PGA5S3 (Simulation, eth_createAccessList)        ── consumed by PLDP23
                                 5FB5MW (Simulation, PathSuppression)             ── composed into M756BN
                                 JTLWA3 (next_base_fee, base_fee_next)            ── consumed cross-epic

INTRA-EPIC (SHT6GE):             M756BN (Dispatcher) ──► HF2R2E (monitor)
                                 M756BN ──► PLDP23 (N6)
                                 G6DNW4 (sign+fee) ──► PLDP23
                                 HF2R2E (monitor) ──► PLDP23
```
`PLDP23` (N6, submit orchestration) gates on `M756BN` + `G6DNW4` + `HF2R2E` + `ZUZANP`
(hard); `HF2R2E` (monitor) gates on `M756BN` (Dispatcher); `JTLWA3` (next_base_fee) is
standalone (pure EVM math; consumed cross-epic by Simulation's `base_fee_next`; referenced
by `G6DNW4`/`PLDP23` for the 1.5x headroom — no hard intra-epic edge, the leaf is called as
a pure fn). `G6DNW4`'s `priority_fee` is consumed off `tx_params` (no hard edge to
`YL2MTH`).

# Scope: Publisher/subscriber → Rust core

Epic `2K2JP4` · Scope task `I7KVKM` · Agent `researcher_1@degenbot`

Status legend: **COMPLETED** = Rust-owned + Python delegating · **IN-FIGHT** = partial (Rust exists, Python still authority somewhere) · **NOT-STARTED** = no Rust counterpart; rubric says belongs in Rust.

Rubric (§2.1) criteria shorthand: **hot** (per-block/per-log?) · **GIL** (CPU-bound holds GIL?) · **type** (pure int/tag vs Python obj/WeakSet) · **I/O** (in-process dispatch vs RPC/DB) · **eco** (Python-ecosystem coupling) · **dup** (§2.3 duplication smell) · **standalone** (ADR-005).

## KEY DISTINCTION (orchestrator's): MECHANISM vs CONSUMERS

- **MECHANISM** = the dispatch/listener infrastructure (subscribe/unregister + fan-out `notify`). Rust ALREADY owns a complete one; the Python `PublisherMixin` is a parallel copy. ⇒ `port-now` to bridge (IN-FIGHT convergence), not greenfield.
- **CONSUMERS** = the Python orchestration that subscribes to drive update loops (engine_registry, CLI update hooks, test fakes). ⇒ `stays-python` (orchestration/drivers), with only the *subscribe call* routed through the Rust seam.

## §2.3 duplication smell — CONFIRMED + already partially resolved

A **complete Rust pub/sub mechanism already exists** in `degenbot-bot`, running on `BotState` in the hot pump loop; Python has a **parallel** mechanism on the (being-phased-out) Python pool classes. They are not bridged:

| Layer | Mechanism | Pointer |
|---|---|---|
| Rust (hot path) | `PoolStateSubscriber: Send+Sync` trait + `LogDispatcher::{subscribe(pool_id, Weak<dyn PoolStateSubscriber>), notify(pool_id), dispatch(log, state)}` — `Weak` fan-out with dead-weak skipping, applied AFTER the `BotState` write guard is released (D2 lock order); `EngineSubscriber` adapts it to `UniswapEngine::insert_dirty`; `DrainSink{on_drain,on_send,notify_block}` for the pump drain lifecycle. | `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/log_dispatcher.rs`; `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/solvers/uniswap_engine/engine_subscriber.rs`; `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/drain_sink.rs` |
| Python (parallel) | `Publisher`/`Subscriber` Protocol + `PublisherMixin` (`subscribe`/`unsubscribe`/`_notify_subscribers` over a `WeakSet`) + `PoolStateMessage`/`...PoolStateUpdated`. Each Python pool calls `self._notify_subscribers(message=...PoolStateUpdated(self.state))` after a state change. | `src/degenbot/types/concrete.py`; consumers: `uniswap/{v2,v3,v4}_liquidity_pool.py`, `aerodrome/pools.py`, `balancer/{pools,stable_pools}.py`, `curve/curve_stableswap_liquidity_pool.py` |

The Rust mechanism is the canonical one per the migration vision (Rust owns state → Rust notifies). The work is **bridging** (a `PySubscriberAdapter` so Python consumers can subscribe to Rust `BotState` notifications through `LogDispatcher`), then retiring the parallel Python `PublisherMixin` dispatch on pool types whose state is Rust-owned.

## COMPLETED (Rust-owned, Python delegates)

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) | Pointer |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rust pub/sub mechanism** (`PoolStateSubscriber` trait + `LogDispatcher` subscribe/notify/dispatch + `Weak`-fan-out + dead-weak skip + D2 lock discipline) | `done` | hot (per-log in pump); GIL-free (`parking_lot::Mutex`, no Python); type=pure (pool_id u64); standalone (a `cargo add degenbot` consumer subscribes to `BotState` updates directly). Already routes `EngineSubscriber`→engine dirty-mark. | `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/log_dispatcher.rs` |
| **Engine subscriber adapter** (`EngineSubscriber` → `UniswapEngine::insert_dirty`) | `done` | the canonical `PoolStateSubscriber` impl; bridges Rust notify→engine dirty-mark. | `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/solvers/uniswap_engine/engine_subscriber.rs` |
| **Pump drain lifecycle notifications** (`DrainSink::on_drain`/`on_send`/`notify_block`) | `done` | hot-path drain fan-out; already Rust. | `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/drain_sink.rs` |

## IN-FIGHT (Rust exists, Python still authority somewhere)

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale | Python side | Rust side | Child task |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Python pool pub/sub dispatch** (`PublisherMixin._notify_subscribers` on V2/V3/V4/Aerodrome/Balancer/Curve pools → `...PoolStateUpdated` messages) | `partial` → bridge + retire | dup (parallel to `LogDispatcher`); hot (per state change). Bridge via a `PySubscriberAdapter` (`#[pyclass] impl PoolStateSubscriber` holding a `Py<PyAny>` Python `Subscriber`/callback; re-acquires GIL on `on_pool_state_updated`); register with `LogDispatcher::subscribe`. Then retire `PublisherMixin` dispatch on Rust-owned pool types. | `src/degenbot/types/concrete.py::{Publisher,Subscriber,PublisherMixin,_notify_subscribers,PoolStateMessage}`; the `_notify_subscribers(message=...)` callsites in the pool classes | `PoolStateSubscriber`+`LogDispatcher` (done) — needs the PyO3 adapter bridging Python subscribers IN | `ZBD4MS` |

## NOT-STARTED (`port-now` / `stays-python`)

| Sub-module | Disposition | Rationale (§2.1) | Python side | Rust side | Child task |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`PySubscriberAdapter` PyO3 seam** (let a Python `Subscriber`/callback register as a `PoolStateSubscriber` with `LogDispatcher`) | `port-now` | thin translator (rubric §3 B); bridges the two mechanism halves. hot-path-adjacent (re-acquires GIL only when a Python subscriber is present). standalone: a Python-driven MEV bot subscribes to Rust state through this. | n/a (the bridge itself) | (adapter lives in `degenbot-python`; cores stay pyo3-free) | `ZBD4MS` (folds the IN-FIGHT bridge above — one task does both) |
| **Python pub/sub consumers** (subscribe-to-drive-update-loop orchestration: `engine_registry` wiring, CLI update hooks, `FakeSubscriber` test helper) | `stays-python` (route subscribe call only) | eco=Python async/CLI orchestration; the *mechanism* is Rust (sibling). Consumer *reaction* bodies stay Python. | `src/degenbot/arbitrage/engine_registry.py`; CLI; `tests/fakes/subscribers.py` | n/a | `73UJL6` (deps `ZBD4MS`) |
| **Stays-Python (recorded, not ported)** | `stays-python` | | | | |
| └ `TextMessage` (generic text pub/sub message) | `stays-python` | Python-only convenience message with no Rust-state equivalent; only `PoolStateMessage`/`PoolStateUpdated` bridges. | `src/degenbot/types/concrete.py::TextMessage` | n/a | — |
| └ RPC WebSocket `eth_subscribe` / `subscribe_blocks` / `subscribe_logs` | `stays-python` (out of scope) | RPC pub-sub — a different concern (Epic for `degenbot-rpc`), NOT this in-process message mechanism. | `src/degenbot/bot.py::subscribe_blocks/subscribe_logs`; `engine_registry.subscribe` | n/a | — |
| └ Consumer orchestration *logic* (what `notify` does in each consumer) | `stays-python` | orchestration/drivers (per §2.1 "Keep in Python"). Routed through the Rust seam (subscribe call), bodies unchanged. | `engine_registry`, CLI update loops | n/a | — |

## Child task split (port-now/partial rows → implementation tasks)

| Child | Title | Disposition origin | Deps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ZBD4MS` | Extend Rust `PoolStateSubscriber`/`LogDispatcher` with a `PySubscriberAdapter` seam; retire parallel Python `PublisherMixin` dispatch on Rust-owned pools | mechanism `port-now` + IN-FIGHT bridge | — (Rust mechanism already landed; in-process, no DB/BotState edge to wire) |
| `73UJL6` | Route Python pub/sub consumers (engine_registry/CLI/test fakes) through the `PySubscriberAdapter` seam; consumer reaction bodies stay Python | consumers `stays-python` (subscribe-call routing only) | `ZBD4MS` (intra-epic) |

Route-before-type ordering: `ZBD4MS` (the bridge seam) → `73UJL6` (consumer subscription routing). The Rust mechanism itself is `done` (no ordering edge to a mechanism-build task — it already exists).

## Open dependency / blocking questions

1. **Cross-epic edges: NONE.** Pub/sub is in-process (no `SLHSM4`/DB edge). `BotState`+`LogDispatcher` are co-located in `degenbot-bot` and already Rust-owned — a `done` reference, not a dep to wire (per your guidance "record as reference if so, no edge"). The `engine_registry`'s `engine.subscribe(node_ws)` is RPC WS-subscribe, unrelated. [RESOLVED — no cross-epic edges to wire.]
2. **Retirement sequencing of `PublisherMixin` on pool classes:** `ZBD4MS` retires the Python dispatch ONLY on pool types whose state is already Rust-owned (`BotState` V2/V3/V4). Pools whose state is still Python-authority (e.g. Balancer/Curve if not yet migrated) keep `PublisherMixin` until their state migrates. `ZBD4MS`'s AC scopes this per-pool-type; flag any pool type whose state isn't yet Rust-owned as "keep Python dispatch" rather than force-retire. [DECIDED — per-pool-type retirement gated on state ownership; non-blocking.]
3. **`PySubscriberAdapter` GIL re-acquisition cost** on the hot path: only fires when a Python subscriber is actually registered for a pool_id (most hot-path pools have only the Rust `EngineSubscriber`, no Python subscriber → no GIL cost). Acceptable; recorded in `ZBD4MS` AC. Non-blocking.
4. **`DrainSink` trait extension for Python consumers?** Decided NO — Python consumers subscribe per-pool via `LogDispatcher::subscribe`, not the `DrainSink` pump-lifecycle trait (which is engine-internal). Keeps the surface minimal. Non-blocking.

## Validation Gates (scope task)
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` — PASS at baseline (confirmed; no cores touched by the scope pass).
- Scope table written + children created before marking done.
- Child tasks `ZBD4MS` / `73UJL6` created with Goal/Context(cited rubric dispositions + the dup-smell + mechanism-vs-consumer distinction)/AC/Validation-Gates/Non-goals; intra-epic edge (`ZBD4MS→73UJL6`) wired; no cross-epic edges (none needed).

Result pointer: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` (also recorded here; `ergo --json show` `result` field may display `None` per the known gotcha — cosmetic).

data.title: degenbot-price core crate: Chainlink latestRoundData/decimals + Aave getAssetPrice readers over degenbot-rpc eth_call
data.body:
## Goal
- Land a new pyo3-free `degenbot-oracle` (or `degenbot-price`) core crate (`rust/crates/degenbot-price/`) owning the **price MECHANISM**: typed readers for on-chain price feeds over `degenbot-rpc`'s typed `eth_call`. Two readers: (1) the **Chainlink aggregator reader** — `ChainlinkPriceFeed { address, chain_id }` with `latest_round_data() -> (round_id, answer, started_at, updated_at, answered_in_round)` + `decimals() -> u8` + a `price() -> U256`/decimal-corrected convenience fn (port of `src/degenbot/chainlink/price_feed.py::ChainlinkPriceContract`); (2) the **Aave oracle reader** — `AavePriceOracle { oracle_address }` with `get_asset_price(asset_address) -> U256` (port of `OraclePriceFetcher.fetch`, the `getAssetPrice(address)` call). Both route their `eth_call` through `degenbot_rpc::Contract::call` (already Rust-owned).

## Context
- Scope task: `XS57NO` (Epic `VNNYI6`). Rubric disposition: **port-now**.
- §2.1 criteria (the mechanism): type=pure Address/int/U256 (the `latestRoundData`/`getAssetPrice` returns + `decimals`); I/O= RPC `eth_call` (pure decode of `int256 answer`/`uint8 decimals`/`uint256 price` → typed value); warm/cool (per valuation sweep — `Erc20Token.price` is read on demand; Aave `OraclePriceFetcher.fetch` per analysis batch, not per-block hot). **standalone**: a `cargo add degenbot` consumer valuing positions needs a Rust price reader. **§2.3 duplication smell: NONE** — `rg 'price|oracle|valuation' rust/crates/` (excluding test oracles + math-port comments) returns zero price/valuation logic; this is greenfield in Rust.
- The underlying `eth_call` primitive IS already Rust-owned: `degenbot_rpc::contract::Contract::call(function_signature, args, block)` returns decoded values; a PyO3 seam `PyAsyncContract` exists in `degenbot-python/src/rpc/`. So a price reader routes through Rust today — no new RPC work needed, reference only.
- Python sources of truth: `src/degenbot/chainlink/price_feed.py::ChainlinkPriceContract` (the `latestRoundData()` + `decimals()` eth_calls + the `answer / 10**decimals` → float); `src/degenbot/aave/analysis/orchestrator.py::OraclePriceFetcher` (the `getAssetPrice(address)` eth_call); `src/degenbot/erc20/erc20.py` `Erc20Token._price_oracle: ChainlinkPriceContract | None` + `price` getter (the per-token mechanism).
- KEY DISTINCTION (orchestrator's): this task = the MECHANISM (feed readers). Consumer valuation orchestration (using prices to rank paths / value positions) = stays-python (sibling task).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New crate `rust/crates/degenbot-price/` (`Cargo.toml` depending on `degenbot-core` + `degenbot-rpc` + `alloy::primitives`; no pyo3), `lib.rs`, modules: `chainlink.rs` (`ChainlinkPriceFeed`, mirroring `ChainlinkPriceContract`), `aave.rs` (`AavePriceOracle`, mirroring `OraclePriceFetcher`).
- `ChainlinkPriceFeed::decimals() -> Result<u8>` + `latest_round_data() -> Result<RoundData>` + `price() -> Result<U256>` (decimal-corrected; offer both raw-int256-answer + decimal-adjusted). `AavePriceOracle::get_asset_price(asset_address) -> Result<U256>` + a bulk `fetch_prices(assets) -> HashMap<Address,U256>` matching `OraclePriceFetcher.fetch`'s tolerant per-asset error handling (skip on `ContractLogicError`, log, continue).
- Both route `eth_call` through `degenbot_rpc::Contract::call` (no re-implementation of RPC).
- `#[cfg(test)]` parity: a fixture RPC mock (or recorded response) returns the same `answer`/`decimals`/`getAssetPrice` values as the Python readers (keep Py as oracle per §4.2).
- **Zero `pyo3`** in the crate (enforced by `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`). Workspace member in `rust/Cargo.toml`.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`.

## Non-goals
- The PyO3 seam + Python cutover of `ChainlinkPriceContract`/`OraclePriceFetcher`/`Erc20Token.price` (sibling task).
- The Aave valuation CONSUMER orchestration (`PositionAnalysisService.analyze_market` ranking by health factor, `price_adjusted_balance`) — stays-python (sibling task; pure calc in `aave/analysis/core.py` stays Python until/unless a math-port epic moves it).
- Reading the `price_source`/oracle-address DB column — that's the Aave rehydrate path (`OKKMG5`, Epic `AZGJUN`); this crate CONSUMES the resolved oracle `Address` (provided by the caller), it doesn't query the DB.
- The RPC `eth_call` primitive itself (`degenbot-rpc::Contract::call`) — already Rust-owned; reference, not a dep to port.
- Path-ranking by USD value / solver valuation — consumer concern, stays-python.

data.title: PyO3 PyChainlinkPriceFeed/PyAavePriceOracle seam; convert ChainlinkPriceContract/OraclePriceFetcher/Erc20Token.price to delegating shells
data.body:
## Goal
- Add a PyO3 seam (`#[pyclass] PyChainlinkPriceFeed` + `#[pyclass] PyAavePriceOracle` in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/oracle/` or `price/`) over the new `degenbot-price` core crate (sibling task), and convert the Python `ChainlinkPriceContract` (`src/degenbot/chainlink/price_feed.py`) and `OraclePriceFetcher` (`src/degenbot/aave/analysis/orchestrator.py`) into delegating shells. `Erc20Token._price_oracle`/`price` (`src/degenbot/erc20/erc20.py`) routes through the Rust `PyChainlinkPriceFeed`.

## Context
- Scope task: `XS57NO` (Epic `VNNYI6`). Rubric disposition: **port-now** (PyO3 seam + Python cutover, rubric §3 B+C).
- §2.1: thin translator (extract args → `py.detach()` the RPC `eth_call` → wrap typed return). The Python `ChainlinkPriceContract`/`OraclePriceFetcher` shells retain their public API (`price` property, `fetch(asset_addresses)`) so callers (`Erc20Token.price`, `PositionAnalysisService.analyze_market`) are unchanged.
- `chainlink/CONTEXT.md` already notes the architecture debt: `ChainlinkPriceContract` reads `self._bot.provider` directly instead of receiving a `ProviderAdapter`/`PoolIO` — this cutover fixes that by routing through the Rust `Contract` (which holds the `AlloyProvider`).
- Deps: sibling `degenbot-price` core crate. The oracle address consumed by `AavePriceOracle` comes from `PositionQuery.get_oracle_address` — once `OKKMG5` (Epic `AZGJUN`) lands, that's a Rust call; until then the Python shell passes the resolved address in. NO hard cross-epic edge.
- KEY DISTINCTION: this task ports the MECHANISM's PyO3 surface. The CONSUMER valuation orchestration (`PositionAnalysisService`, path-ranking) stays-python (sibling task).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `#[pyclass] PyChainlinkPriceFeed { address, chain_id }` with `decimals`/`latest_round_data`/`price` mirroring `ChainlinkPriceContract`'s properties; `#[pyclass] PyAavePriceOracle { oracle_address }` with `fetch(asset_addresses) -> dict[Address,int]` matching `OraclePriceFetcher.fetch`'s shape + tolerant error handling. Registered in `c_api.rs`; `py.detach()` for the RPC I/O.
- Python `ChainlinkPriceContract` (and `chainlink/__init__.py`) delegates to `PyChainlinkPriceFeed`; the inline `provider.call_raw`/`abi_decode` bodies deleted. `OraclePriceFetcher.fetch` delegates to `PyAavePriceOracle`; the inline `raw_call`/`encode_function_calldata` loop deleted.
- `Erc20Token._price_oracle` becomes `PyChainlinkPriceFeed` (or a Python `ChainlinkPriceContract` shell wrapping it); `Erc20Token.price` getter unchanged signature.
- Parity (§4.2): `ChainlinkPriceContract.price` + `OraclePriceFetcher.fetch` against a fixture/mock RPC return identical values as the prior Python path (Py as oracle until green, retire per §4.3). `tests/test_chainlink_price_feed.py` + the Aave analysis tests pass.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-python`, `just test-python` (`tests/test_chainlink_price_feed.py`, `tests/erc20/test_erc20_token.py`, Aave analysis suite), `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`, `just lint-rust`, `just lint-python`.

## Non-goals
- The `degenbot-price` core crate (sibling task).
- The Aave valuation CONSUMER (`PositionAnalysisService.analyze_market`, `core.py` calc) — stays-python (sibling task).
- Reading the `price_source` DB column (Epic `AZGJUN`/`OKKMG5`) — this seam takes the resolved oracle `Address` as an arg.
- Path-ranking by USD value / solver USD valuation — consumer concern.

data.title: Solidly oracle retirement — delete SolidlyStableSolver + solvers/__init__ re-export + test_engine_vs_solidly_parity.py (§4.3 delete-together; production confirmed Rust-only)
data.body:
## Goal
- **Retire the Solidly parity oracle** per rubric §4.3 oracle-retirement protocol: delete
  the Python `SolidlyStableSolver` (`src/degenbot/arbitrage/solvers/solidly_stable.py`) +
  its `solvers/__init__.py` re-export + the parity test
  `tests/arbitrage/test_engine_vs_solidly_parity.py` TOGETHER (delete the parity oracle WITH
  its parity tests — do not leave an equivalence harness comparing two live implementations).
- Pre-conditions confirmed: the production Solidly solve path is fully Rust
  (`solve_solidly_path_int` in `degenbot-bot/src/solvers/uniswap_engine/solver_dispatch.rs`),
  and `SolidlyStableSolver` is referenced ONLY by its own definition + the parity test +
  COMMENT docstrings in the Rust solver_dispatch.rs (port provenance) — NOT on the
  production solve path.

## Context
- Scope task: `EB5M6V` (epic `M6QUG6`), row R1.
- Rubric disposition: `port-now` (§4.3 oracle-retirement cleanup, NOT a port). Per §4.3:
  "When the Rust port is byte-for-byte verified and the routing lands, delete the Python
  parity oracle TOGETHER with its parity tests." The Rust Solidly solve (`solve_solidly_path_int`)
  is the production path; `SolidlyStableSolver` survived ONLY as the parity oracle (per
  `src/degenbot/arbitrage/CONTEXT.md` "Solidly Solver *(parity oracle only)*" +
  `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` Fork B "Disposition:
  `SolidlyStableSolver` moves from `stays-python` → parity oracle only").
- Pre-condition checks CONFIRMED (read-only research):
  - Production = Rust: `rg SolidlyStableSolver` in `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/` returns
    only COMMENT docstrings (`solver_dispatch.rs`: "Faithful port of
    `arbitrage.solvers.solidly_stable.SolidlyStableSolver`") — NOT a runtime import.
  - `SolidlyStableSolver` referenced ONLY by: its own file (`solidly_stable.py`),
    `solvers/__init__.py` (re-export + `__all__`), the parity test
    (`test_engine_vs_solidly_parity.py`), + CONTEXT.md. NO production callsite.
  - The parity gate `FEMZJC` is green (Solidly epic `MS5MBQ`/`FWTUOQ` done).
- Canonical references: `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` §4.3
  (oracle-retirement protocol) + Fork B, `src/degenbot/arbitrage/CONTEXT.md`
  ("parity oracle only"), `rust/CONTEXT.md` ("Exception — SolidlyStableSolver: ...
  survives as a parity oracle only — Not on the production solve path").

## Acceptance Criteria
- Delete `src/degenbot/arbitrage/solvers/solidly_stable.py` (the whole file —
  `SolidlyStableSolver` class + `GOLDEN_SECTION_ITERATIONS`).
- Remove the `SolidlyStableSolver` import + `__all__` entry from
  `src/degenbot/arbitrage/solvers/__init__.py`.
- Delete `tests/arbitrage/test_engine_vs_solidly_parity.py` (the whole file — per §4.3
  the parity test retires WITH the oracle).
- Update `src/degenbot/arbitrage/CONTEXT.md`: change the "Solidly Solver" row from
  "parity oracle only" → REMOVED (record the retirement; the `solve_solidly_path_int`
  production entry stays).
- Update `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` Fork B if it references the
  surviving parity oracle as a current state (note the retirement — the fork is historical
  record; the disposition line "parity oracle only" becomes "retired").
- Update the Rust `solver_dispatch.rs` COMMENT docstrings that cite
  `arbitrage.solvers.solidly_stable.SolidlyStableSolver` as a living reference (the port
  provenance is now historical — keep the comment as a "ported from" note OR drop it; no
  runtime impact).
- `rg SolidlyStableSolver` over `src/` + `tests/` returns zero hits (COMMENT-only Rust hits
  are acceptable historical provenance).
- `just test-all` green (the Solidly parity test deletion must not break the test suite —
  the standalone `tests/arbitrage/test_engine_vs_brent_parity.py` retains Brent oracle
